movies.title: A Grin Without A Cat
movies.description: This epic film-essay from Chris Marker ( La Jetée ) investigates the worldwide political wars of the ‘60s and ‘70s, especially the emergence of the New Left. Originally released in 1978, BAM is delighted to show the restored and “re-actualized” version Marker released after the fall of the Soviet Union 15 years later. Described by Marker as "scenes of the Third World War," the film interweaves imagery of Lewis Carroll's Cheshire Cat in an indictment of the leftist movement’s unfortunate failure to manifest meaningful change. Whereas Vineland tracks the story of a fictional left wing revolutionary, Marker’s film traces the movement’s real successes and failures in the West.

movies.title: A Litany For Survival: The Life And Work Of Audre Lorde
movies.description: This epic portrait of the award-winning Black lesbian poet, mother, teacher, and activist Audre Lorde catalogs an incredibly impactful, revolutionary career. From her childhood roots in Harlem to her battle with breast cancer, the film explores a life, and a body of work, that bridged the Civil Rights movement, the women’s movement, and the struggle for lesbian and gay rights. New restoration premier; Q&A to follow with Ada Gay Griffin, Michelle Parkerson & J.T. Takagi

movies.title: A Matter Of Life And Death
movies.description: Haya grew up in the shadow of a curse’s promise that she would die at 30. After a series of failed attempts to end her life—an effort to take her fate into her own hands—she crosses paths with a brilliant but emotionally withdrawn surgeon. Youssef, who suffers from an abnormally slow heartbeat and only truly feels alive when he's operating and holding a scalpel, might be just who Haya has been looking for. Her request that Youssef kill her kicks off a flowering relationship, and a surprisingly uplifting exploration of the existential struggles that plague so many on the precipice of entering their thirties.

movies.title: A Night With Alex Tatarsky
movies.description: The word cinema is an abbreviation of the French cinématographe , a term coined by the Lumière Brothers, who combined the Greek words for “movement” and “writing” to describe this new form of expression. As part of Triple Canopy Presents: Magic, Alex Tatarsky—2025 Triple Canopy fellow—will share a local clown’s take on “movement writing.” Tatarsky will present research and workshop characters live with the audience for a new piece of fiction that considers American traditions of conjuring and spirit channeling in the lineage of experimental improvisational performance. Part lecture, part seance, Tatarsky’s performance draws on the researcher and artist Shannon Taggart’s investigations into spectral photography and “spirit cinema” to investigate the life of objects and the material of spirit.

movies.title: A Prayer for the Dying
movies.description: Jacob, a Danish immigrant still haunted by his experiences in the Civil War, has built a new life in the town of Friendship. Serving as both priest and sheriff, he is called to retrieve a body found just beyond the town limits and escorts a disoriented woman, discovered wandering in a nearby field, back to the local doctor. After examining the corpse, the doctor warns Jacob that the man may have been carrying diphtheria. The woman may also be infected. When her husband arrives to take her home, the doctor attempts to warn him about the risk of contagion, but the man refuses to listen.Fearing an outbreak, the doctor urges Jacob to keep the diagnosis secret to prevent the townsfolk from panicking and trying to leave town. After Jacob suffers a personal loss, the doctor orders a quarantine just as a devastating bushfire changes course toward the town. Determined to protect the people in his care, Jacob is pushed to his breaking point. Trapped between a deadly epidemic and the approaching inferno, and having lost nearly everything he holds dear, Jacob struggles to preserve both the town and his own sanity.Based on Stewart O’Nan’s novel of the same name, Dara Van Dusen’s debut feature is nothing short of a gem—one that deserves to be experienced on the big screen. The film's assured direction, outstanding performances, and breathtaking cinematography immerse viewers in an apocalyptic story where the true threat isn't zombies or monsters, but the devastating consequences of human fear, ignorance, and poor decisions. It is a vision of hell on earth, set in a time when a single mistake could prove fatal and there was no turning back. (ANNICK MAHNERT)

movies.title: A Pure Person: The Sonic Landscape Of Lim Giong
movies.description: Programmed by Frank Yan Co-presented by CineCina Few artists have shaped the sound of contemporary cinema as quietly, or as profoundly, as Lim Giong. His soundscapes breathe, drift, pulse, and haunt the films they inhabit. Tracing a remarkable three-decade evolution from Taiwanese rock icon to one of Chinese-language cinema’s most essential composers, this retrospective follows Lim’s sonic journey from Taipei to the mainland and the borderlands beyond. Highlighting defining collaborations with auteurs like Hou Hsiao-hsien, Jia Zhang-ke, and Bi Gan, and featuring his personal artistic inspirations (Pink Floyd’s The Wall ), this series celebrates a towering cultural force who maps modern history through rhythm, texture, and memory.

movies.title: A Sad And Beautiful World
movies.description: Across three decades of passion, loss, and hope, Nino and Yasmina are bound by a magnetic relationship. Torn between love and survival, the reunited childhood sweethearts must decide whether to build a family and seek happiness in Lebanon, or leave their home amid the country’s unfolding tragedies. A heartfelt portrayal of resilience, A Sad and Beautiful World made its world premiere at Venice Days, where it won the People’s Choice Award. Followed by a Q&A with director Cyril Aris

movies.title: A Tribe Called Love
movies.description: New York Premiere In a Somali neighbourhood in Toronto, innocent teenagers Farah and Halima fall in love. But both have been warned to stay away from each other because they are from different tribes. When Farah's family moves to Vancouver because of a neighbourhood tragedy, the young lovers are torn apart. Their romance rekindles in their 20s when they reunite in Toronto. That is, until the same cultural barriers that once divided them resurface. Will their love be enough to rewrite their fate, or are some tragedies destined to repeat themselves? This modern-day Romeo and Juliet cautionary tale explores whether cultural barriers can be broken once and for all. A Tribe Called Love is told with the pop, bang and pizzazz of Scott Pilgrim vs The World , mixed with the tension, comedy, and tightly-knit neighbourhood of Spike Lee's Do The Right Thing . Winner of the Audience Choice Award at the 2025 Reelworld Film Festival. May 22 screening followed by a Q&A with director Mohamed Ahmed, producer Andy Marshall, and cast—moderated by Muna Mohamed

movies.title: A Tribute To Assata: Eyes Of The Rainbow
movies.description: After escaping from prison in 1979, the revolutionary, thinker, and Black Panther and Black Liberation Army leader Assata Shakur found political asylum in Cuba, where she lived in exile for over 40 years. Gloria Rolando’s Eyes of the Rainbow finds Shakur in Havana discussing life before and after exile and her own Afro-Cuban roots. Weaving together Shakur’s spiritual connection to the Yoruba Orisha Oya, her militant political commitments and an Afro-diasporic tapestry of music, Rolando dedicated the documentary to “all women who struggle for a better world.” Assata Shakur joined the ancestors on September 25, 2025 and the screening will be an occasion for remembrance centered on her lifelong devotion to freedom from all forms of oppression. The screening will be followed by a conversation with series programmer Yasmina Price, organizer Monifa Bandele and filmmaker Yaania Bell about collective struggle, memory, and the intertwinement of culture and militancy.

movies.title: Abraham Lincoln
movies.description: This pre-Hays Code biopic from D. W. Griffith ( The Birth of a Nation ) follows the life of Abraham Lincoln, chronicling his early years as a country lawyer and romance with Ann Rutledge through to his presidency and later assasination. This hushed film, far from the rousing American mythmaking of John Ford’s Young Mister Lincoln or Griffith’s own Americana, depicts a Lincoln (portrayed brilliantly by Walter Huston—who also plays the Devil in All That Money Can Buy ) haunted by past tragedy and fated to an early demise.

movies.title: ACE Presents: Rosemary's Baby
movies.description: Q&A with film historian Bobbie O’Steen moderated by music editor Suzana Peric on Saturday, October 24th

movies.title: Aerograd
movies.description: Introduction by programmer Edo Choi on Saturday, October 17th

movies.title: Afro-Cuban Music
movies.description: Through experimental polemics, observational studies and historical investigations, these inventive documentaries explore the African roots of Cuban music through the intersection of cultural and political struggle. NOW! (1965) Dir. Santiago Alvarez 6min, DCP Influential Cuban filmmaker Santiago Alvarez combines footage of police brutality and Black Liberation from the 60s Civil Rights movement, scored by Lena Horne’s urgent musical call to action in a radical montage. Habana Solo (2000) Dir. Juan Carlos Alom 15min, Digital A city symphony in miniature, Alom’s powerful short juxtaposes Havana’s streets and peoples and the music of Afro-Cuban street performers. Y . . . tenemos sabor (1967) Dir. Sara Gómez 30min, DCP Following pioneering Rumba musician Alberto Zayas, this dynamic documentary takes us through the history of Cuban music. A Short Radiography of Hip Hop in Cuba (2004) Dir. Ricardo Bacallao 21min, DCP A look at the history of hip-hop culture in Cuba through the eyes of Rodolfo Rensoli, founder of the Cuban Hip Hop Festival.

movies.title: After Hours
movies.description: When office worker Paul Hackett (Dunne) embarks on a seemingly innocuous journey downtown to meet up with a mysterious woman (Arquette) he met at a coffee shop hours earlier, her surreal behavior is just the first of many surprises. As the night unravels, this portrait of 1980s SoHo follows Hackett into Berlin-themed nightclubs, the apartment of a distressed waitress (Teri Garr), and the ice cream truck of a do-gooder driver (Catherine O’Hara). This early-career Scorsese masterpiece—anchored by Michael Ballhaus’ frantic cinematography—toes the line between haunting and absurd as increasingly higher stakes prevent Hackett’s simple journey: to get home.

movies.title: After Oil
movies.description: Across Algeria, South Africa, and Kenya, communities and refugee camps confront the realities of the global energy transition. Stories of resistance to fossil fuel extraction on indigenous land, the unequal distribution of energy infrastructure in cities, and grassroots struggles for self-determination in resource-exploited regions intertwine to reveal the human stakes of energy policy. Together, these perspectives illuminate the broader political, environmental, and social challenges shaping Africa in the green energy transition. Followed by a Q&A with director Boima Tucker

movies.title: Afterimage
movies.cast: Bogusław Linda

movies.title: Alam
movies.description: Tamer, a Palestinian living in Israel, leads the life of a typical high school student until the beautiful Maysaa​​’ arrives. Hoping to impress her, he agrees to take part in a mysterious operation to covertly raise the Palestinian flag and peacefully disrupt local celebrations on the eve of Israel’s Independence Day—a day of mourning for Palestinians. Unsure of his own convictions, Tamer must determine what matters to him. A skillful examination of the fraught political awakening young Palestinians are forced to undergo, this striking debut feature film from Firas Khoury “perfectly captures teenage fearlessness and bravado along with a certain cluelessness about how the real world works” ( Variety ).

movies.title: Alien: Resurrection
movies.description: The fourth entry in the Alien series brings Sigourney Weaver’s Lt. Ellen Ripley, last seen swan diving into a vat of molten steel, back from the Great Beyond—after a fashion, at least. Cloned from samples of extraterrestrial-contaminated DNA, Ripley…

movies.title: All Dirt Roads Taste Of Salt
movies.description: The feature debut from writer-director Raven Jackson, All Dirt Roads Taste of Salt serves as a decade-spanning portrait of Mack, a Black woman in Mississippi. With minimal dialogue and breathtaking cinematography from Jomo Fray ( Nickel Boys ), the sparse, unhurried film weaves alternately through love and heartbreak, joy and sorrow, connection and loss in a stunning dedication to the experience of being alive. The July 25 screening followed by a Q&A with Raven Jackson.

movies.title: All That Heaven Allows
movies.description: Perhaps the very finest of Sirk’s Ross Hunter-produced melodramas, All That Heaven Allows pairs Jane Wyman and Rock Hudson as, respectively, a well-off widow in country club Connecticut, and the broad-necked, Thoreau-reading gardener who she falls for.…

movies.title: All That Money Can Buy (Aka The Devil And Daniel Webster)
movies.description: In 1840, hardworking farmer Jabez Stone is broke and plagued by seemingly pre-ordained bad luck. After a series of mishaps cement his tough streak, his impulsive declaration that he would sell his soul to the devil manifests the personification of evil himself (a mischievous, terrifying Walter Huston—who also plays the eponymous role in D. W. Griffith’s Abraham Lincoln ) offering good luck in exchange. As Stone’s ill-begotten luck improves and his wealth mounts, he transforms into an increasingly sinister husband, son, and community member. Originally released as All That Money Can Buy but later dubbed The Devil and Daniel Webster , this supernatural thriller unpacks the nefarious nature of wealth.

movies.title: All That’S Left Of You
movies.description: A deeply moving, multigenerational drama, All That’s Left of You follows a Palestinian teenager who gets swept into a protest in the Occupied West Bank and experiences a moment of violence that rocks his family. The film unfolds as his mother recounts the political and emotional threads that led to that fateful moment. Spanning seven decades, the film—Jordan’s official selection for the 98th Academy Awards—traces the hopes and heartaches of one uprooted family, bearing witness to the scars of dispossession and the enduring legacy of survival. Followed by a Q&A with director & actor Cherien Dabis and actor Adam Bakri.

movies.title: All the President's Men
movies.description: Q&A with Carl Bernstein and Maggie Haberman, White House correspondent for The New York Times, moderated by Natalie Kitroeff of “The Daily” on Sunday, October 18th

movies.title: All We Imagine as Light
movies.description: Winner of the Grand Prix at the 2024 Cannes Film Festival, Kapadia’s fiction feature debut concerns itself with the intimate, everyday concerns of Kani Kusruti and Divya Prabha as Prabha and Anu, roommates and co-workers at a Mumbai hospital, and their…

movies.title: Alma Punk (Punk Soul)
movies.description: Like Nadie es Innocente , Minter’s 1991 film Alma Punk combines improvisation and non-actors in a uniquely produced exploration of Mexico City’s punk scene. Starring a cast led by real-life punk Ana Hernandez (as Alma, which also means “soul”), Alma Punk traces the tortuous path of a young riot grrl from the Mexico City punk scene as she moves north to Tijuana and, eventually, towards the United States. It confidently breaks with the rules of staging docudrama with an unsparing look at Alma’s love life, unfakeable scene bohemianism, and extensive location footage of Mexico before NAFTA and after the 1985 earthquake.

movies.title: Almost Famous
movies.description: Introduction by Jon Caramanica and Joe Coscarelli of “Popcast” on Friday, October 16th

movies.title: Alpha
movies.description: Life swiftly starts to unravel for Alpha and her single mom after the rebellious 13-year-old comes home with a stick-and-poke tattoo made with a used needle at a house party—a mark that may be related to a contagious blood-borne disease that turns its victims into disintegrating stone. The third feature by French director and screenwriter Julia Ducournau, winner of the Palme d’Or at the 2021 Cannes Film Festival for Titane , is a mysterious, unsettling allegory for the 1980s AIDS crisis and the waves of hysteria, prejudice, and exclusion it produced.

movies.title: Alphaville
movies.description: A brilliant mashup of dystopian sci-fi, French New Wave, and 1950s American pulp noir. Jean-Luc Godard’s idiosyncratic feature follows hard-boiled private eye Lemmy Caution (Eddie Constantine, who had already played the character for a decade in less avant-garde fare) in his mission to capture or kill Professor von Braun, creator of the fascist computer Alpha 60 that rules the grim city of Alphaville. With the help of Natacha von Braun (Anna Karina), the professor’s computer programmer daughter, Caution rages against the machine with the ineffably human qualities of love and poetry. Hailed for its unique take on pulp fiction and sci-fi, Alphaville won the prestigious Golden Bear at the 1965 Berlin International Film Festival.

movies.title: Amazing Grace
movies.description: Captured over two transcendent nights in 1972, Amazing Grace brings Aretha Franklin home to the New Temple Missionary Baptist Church in Los Angeles for a legendary gospel performance. With the congregation singing, swaying, clapping, and testifying alongside her, Franklin transforms the church into a space of collective release and ecstatic communion. The film’s intimacy—its sweat, tears, and sheer physical presence—makes music feel less like something performed than something lived. Directed by Sydney Pollack and finally released decades after it was shot, Amazing Grace is a testament to an artist of earth-shaking talent, and a celebration of Black musical and spiritual traditions as a source of joy and collective power. All hail the Queen of Soul.

movies.title: Amreeka
movies.description: The debut feature film by New York-based Palestinian-American director Cherien Dabis, nominated for an Emmy for her work on Only Murders in the Building , tells the story of Muna Farah (Nisreen Faour), a Palestinian divorcée who wins a green card lottery and moves to rural Illinois with her teenage son, Fadi (Melkar Muallem). Anticipating a better life, mother and son arrive at the beginning of the US invasion of Iraq, and have to learn how to deal with a new land, assimilated relatives, and life as an Arab immigrant in post-9/11 America.

movies.title: An Autumn Afternoon
movies.description: Ozu’s gorgeous 53rd and final feature is a return to a favorite theme, the poignant comedy of marriage, with beloved regular Chishu Ryu as a father giving away his daughter and preparing for another, final goodbye. Good Morning’s satire of creeping…

movies.title: An Autumn's Tale
movies.description: Newly arrived in New York City from Hong Kong and unhappily reunited with boyfriend Danny Chan, Jennifer (Cherie Chung) finds a guide to this strange new world in the person of distant relation Samuel Pang, aka “Sampan” (Chow Yun-fat, at his most…

movies.title: Ana
movies.description: The second docufiction collaboration between Reis and Cordeiro, and perhaps the most narratively grounded, Ana follows its titular elderly matriarch and her family in Portugal’s Trás-os-Montes region. In its dedication to Ana as subject, she contains a multiplicity, representing a vibrant tapestry of nature and tradition woven into the region’s daily life.

movies.title: Antigone
movies.description: Brecht’s adaptation of Sophocles’s Antigone—concerning the title character’s rebellion against the uncle, King Creon, who has condemned her to death—is performed in its entirety in Straub and Huillet’s final film set in the ancient world,…

movies.title: Appofeniacs
movies.description:
From writer-director Chris Marrs Piliero comes a psychological horror about the weaponization of deepfake technology – and the disintegration of truth in a digital-first culture. One app. One click. One life, ruined or ended.
As a single piece of synthetic media metastasizes across feeds, the line between what happened and what was generated stops mattering. The film asks the only question left: if everyone will believe it, does the truth need you to?

movies.title: Arco
movies.description: In the year 2075, a 10-year-old girl witnesses a mysterious boy in a rainbow suit fall from the sky. Arco comes from an idyllic far future where time travel is possible. Iris shelters him, and will do whatever it takes to help him return to his time. In return, Arco gives Iris hope for an optimistic future. Directed by author and comic-book illustrator Ugo Bienvenu, this vivacious animated feature debuted at Cannes and won recognition from the New York Film Critics Online and Lumière Awards alongside dozens of prestigious nominations. Academy Award nominee, Best Animated Feature

movies.title: Arsenal
movies.description: Live musical accompaniment by Fima Chupakhin, piano & synths, and Fabio Rojas, percussion, on Sunday, October 11th

movies.title: Art Cinema for Tots: How to Play a Film
movies.description: Born out of a commitment to the idea that it’s never too early to introduce kids to the pleasures of movies made outside of the commercial mainstream—and the suspicion that young audiences are often more open-minded and curious than their elders when…

movies.title: Arteeast Presents Prince Of Nothingwood
movies.description: Co-presented with ArteEast Sonia Kronlund follows Salim Shaheen, the most prolific actor-director-producer in Afghanistan, as he leaves Kabul to shoot his 111th film (or maybe 114th? He’s lost count). In tow is the director’s trusty troupe of delightful outcasts, each more eccentric than the last, determined to make films by whatever means necessary—even if it means dodging landmines and firing live ammunition to get the shot. In conjunction with ArteEast, we’re thrilled to screen Kronlund’s “magical and intrepid” ( The Guardian ) Prince of Nothingwood for one night only on March 3. Stay after the screening for filmmaker Arsalan Danish in conversation with Moshtari Hilal and Parwana Haydar of the Afghan Visual Arts & History Collective

movies.title: Arthouse Sci-Fi
movies.description: Programmed by Jesse Trussell In the overwhelming heat of August, what’s better than going to a chilly theater and watching a big sci-fi movie? We’re doing summer theater escapism BAM style, with arthouse spins on the space saga, time travel, technology run amok, and visitors from another world. Featuring films by Jean-Luc Godard, Andrei Tarkovsky, Chris Marker, John Akomfrah, Apichatpong Weerasethakul, Wong Kar-wai, David Cronenberg, Andrzej Żuławski, and more—come beat the heat with some high-art genre flicks.

movies.title: Arzé
movies.description: Mira Shaib’s feature debut follows Arzé (Abou Abboud), a single mother in Beirut attempting to expand her business selling homemade pies. To afford a delivery scooter, she steals her sister’s beloved bracelet, only to have the scooter stolen the same day. Arzé and her son embark on a journey navigating through the bustling neighborhoods of Beirut to find what they’ve lost as guilt and pressure mount.

movies.title: Ashley Clark Presents: Selections From The World Of Black Film
movies.description: In this thematically and geographically expansive program, writer, curator, and former BAM Director of Film Programming Ashley Clark presents an eclectic selection of works featured in his new book, The World of Black Film: A Journey Through Cinematic Blackness in 100 Films (Laurence King Publishing), a thought-provoking survey of important and influential international Black movies. From Harlem to Rio de Janeiro, Kingston to Dakar, and far beyond, these singular and enthralling films explore the complementary, contrasting, and frequently interconnected experiences and histories of Black people around the globe. Series programmer Ashley Clark will introduce the opening night screening of Daughters of the Dust and sign his new book, The World of Black Film .

movies.title: Assassination
movies.description: 35mm print imported from Japan (courtesy of the Japan Foundation) “Near the end of Japan’s feudal era, Ronin Hachiro Kiyokawa, a smart but shady leader working for the Shogunate, is being secretly watched by a spy ready to kill him if he switches sides. As violence grows between rival political groups, the film digs into themes of loyalty, power, and deception. Its non-linear flashback style keeps Kiyokawa’s true motives unclear. The film stands out as an important part of the Japanese New Wave movement, and Tetsurō Tamba gives a subtle, mysterious performance as Kiyokawa.” - Shun Inoue

movies.title: Atlantics
movies.description: In this neocolonialist zombie folktale, Ada (Sane) sacrifices her passion for Souleiman (Traore), a handsome construction worker broken by wage theft, in exchange for security with a man she neither loves nor desires. After Souleiman and his fellow laborers are lost to the Atlantic during a desperate attempt to seek work in Europe, their spectral forms appear to the abandoned girls of Dakar, who develop a sweating sickness, burning through the city, possessed. Mati Diop’s debut feature and Cannes Grand Prix winner is a ghost tale soaked in longing and rage, moving fluidly between romance, police procedural, supernatural horror, and tender coming-of-age story. Buoyed by Fatima Al Qadiri’s haunting score, Atlantics is at once a delirious fever dream and a sharp indictment of economic exploitation.

movies.title: Atonement (2026)
movies.cast: Boyd Holbrook, Hiam Abbass, Kenneth Branagh
movies.description: Displaced from their home by U.S. military action during the early days of the Iraq War, the Khachaturian family finds refuge with relatives, gathering their three generations together under one roof. But when another bombing erupts nearby, they decide to return to their home across the city. As they navigate the war-torn streets of Baghdad, the family is trapped in a firefight between U.S. Marines and insurgents, and one Marine’s split-second decision devastates the family. Years later, haunted by his time in Iraq and aided by a New Yorker journalist, the Marine seeks to reconcile with the Khachaturian matriarch and her surviving family members. Anchored by moving, unforgettable performances from Boyd Holbrook, Hiam Abbass, and Kenneth Branagh, Atonement is a powerfully human story about the immeasurable costs of war, exploring universal questions about guilt, redemption, and the nature of forgiveness.

movies.title: Autumn Sonata
movies.description: Ingmar and Ingrid, Bergman and Bergman, together at last. Sweden’s most popular export before the Volvo, in her final screen role, plays a world-renowned concert pianist who returns home to reunite with her now-married daughter (Liv Ullmann), long a…

movies.title: Avengers Endgame: Encore
movies.description:
The epic conclusion to the Infinity Saga returns to theaters as AVENGERS ENDGAME: Encore on September 25, 2026. 
After devastating events wiped out half the world’s population, the remaining heroes struggle to move forward. Ultimately, they must come together to restore order and harmony in the universe and bring their loved ones back in a dramatic showdown against Thanos.

movies.title: Babylon
movies.description: Franco Rosso's incendiary Babylon had its world premiere at Cannes in 1980, but went unreleased in the US on account of being “too controversial, and likely to incite racial tension" ( Time Out ). The film follows a young dancehall DJ in South London as he pursues his musical ambitions but seems to experience racism and xenophobia at every turn. Set to a sizzling reggae and lover’s rock soundtrack, Babylon is unapologetically raw and unsentimental, but also tempered by the hazy bliss of the dancehall, where one can release the heat of daily indignities, and music becomes both refuge and resistance. A landmark of Black British cinema, Babylon is a furious, sensual portrait of cultural survival under systemic oppression.

movies.title: Backrooms
movies.description: Drawing on the deep dread of so-called “liminal” spaces—the non-places of depopulated office buildings and parking lots of late capitalist America—this feature debut from 20-year-old Kane Parsons was inspired by a sprawling fictional location first chronicled in a 2019 4chan thread. A simple premise straight out of the internet age snowballs into psychological terror as store-owner Clark (Chiwetel Ejiofor) and his therapist (Renate Reinsve) venture into an unknown dimension through a strange doorway that has appeared in the basement of a furniture showroom.

movies.title: Bacurau
movies.description: Out in the blistering Brazilian sertão, the tiny town of Bacurau has bigger problems than heat, water shortages, and a mayor who treats his constituents like garbage. After their beloved matriarch dies, the villagers discover their home has vanished from the map… and yet some very strange and vaguely threatening tourists have descended upon the town-that-was. What starts as a sun-baked mystery curdles into a blood-soaked saga of colonialism and its consequences, class warfare, and collective revenge. Kleber Mendonça Filho ( Neighboring Sounds , Aquarius ) delivers a daring work of sociopolitical commentary, winning the Jury Prize at the Cannes Film Festival, in this gloriously weird genre mash-up that serves as a critique of contemporary Brazilian society.

movies.title: Bakri Family Shorts Program
movies.description: In addition to their distinguished careers in feature films, members of the Bakri family have appeared in numerous short films spanning a variety of visions and styles. This collection of representative shorts—including one in which Ziad Bakri directs his father and brother—illuminates facets of everyday Palestinian life and more. The Salt Fisherman (2011) Dir. Ziad Bakri 18min With Mohammad Bakri, Saleh Bakri A fisherman lives alone, rising with the sun and carrying his anxieties and tools to the sea, where he works. What's behind his days? Upshot (2024) Dir. Maha Haj 34min With Mohammad Bakri, Areen Omari, Ala Hlehel Suleiman and Mona lead a solitary life caring for animals and trees, and have constant heated discussions about their children’s life choices. Their routine is disturbed when a stranger shows up one day, calling to mind a painful past. The Present (2020) Dir. Farah Nabulsi 24min With Saleh Bakri, Mariam Kanj, Mariam Basha A father and his daughter set out to buy his wife a gift for their wedding anniversary, but are soon confronted by a military checkpoint. Mare Nostrum (2016) Dirs. Rana Kazkaz and Anas Khalaf 13min With Ziad Bakri, Zayn Khalaf On a Mediterranean shore, a Syrian father makes a decision that puts his daughter’s life at risk.

movies.title: Bam | Arteeast Presents: My Father And Qaddafi
movies.description: Jihan’s father Mansur Rashid Kikhia was the Foreign Minister of Libya, ambassador to the United Nations, and a human rights lawyer. After serving in Qaddafi's increasingly brutal regime, he defected from the government and became the leader of the peaceful opposition. For many, Kikhia was a rising star who could have been the next leader of Libya. In 1993, he disappeared from his hotel in Egypt. Jihan’s mother Baha Al Omary, a strong-willed Syrian-American artist, began searching for him, launching the family into an international political maze. Her mission to find justice brought her to the Libyan desert in the middle of the night, face to face with Qaddafi to negotiate her husband’s release. Yet it wasn’t until after the regime’s fall, 19 years later, that his body was found in a freezer near Qaddafi’s palace. My Father and Qaddafi takes the audience on a raw and reflective journey as Jihan pieces together a father she barely remembers, while discovering the troubled history and politics of Libya. Her journey starts from fading personal memories, leading to encounters with family members, her father’s peers, and historical archive footage. Hoping at first to uncover the truth, Jihan instead transforms the mystery into a curiosity that brings her closer to her father and her Libyan identity. She approaches politics not as a distant subject, but as a lived experience that penetrates into every human relationship—even between a little girl and her father. Screening will be followed by a discussion.

movies.title: Barbarella
movies.description: In the 41st century, astronaut Barbarella (Fonda) is tasked with finding Dr. Durand Durand, a scientist the Earth’s government believes to be developing a weapon that could signal the end of humanity. In a 98 minute run-time littered with sensationally campy set design and vibrant costuming, Barbarella’s quest sends her from planet to planet in this ‘60s signature cult film.

movies.title: Bardi
movies.description: Filmmaker and photographer Tala Hadid immersed herself in the rugged, fraternal world of a group of horse-riders in central Morocco for this visually rapturous work that merges portraiture and fabulation. With thrilling camerawork, Hadid accompanies the men as they take part in Tbourida, an equestrian military ritual that dates to the 16th century and allows them to transform into new personas. As the itinerant group rides across the country, Hadid captures with a mix of intimacy and epic grandeur their geographically expansive yet emotionally enclosed universe, with its codes of behavior and fully embodied performances of masculinity. Hadid, whose previous films include the short Y our Dark Hair Ihsan (NYFF43) and the feature House in the Fields , about the Amazigh of Morocco, is fascinated with how people within communities encounter tradition, myth, and the self; Bardi is a majestic work of earthy imagination that transcends time and landscape. Followed by a Q&A with Tala Hadid

movies.title: Beetlejuice
movies.description: With her delivery of the line “My whole life is a dark room… One. Big. Dark. Room,” Winona Ryder cemented herself as a goth girl heroine for the ages, a brooding teen in widow’s weeds relocated by her parents to a creaky country house that happens…

movies.title: Beetlejuice
movies.description:
Tim Burton had made a name for himself with PEE-WEE'S BIG ADVENTURE, but he really captured everyone's attention with the surprise smash BEETLEJUICE in 1988. The movie was so weird Warner Bros. was almost afraid to spring it on an unsuspecting public. But when they did, audiences went wild for it.
The film also gave substantial boosts to the careers of Alec Baldwin (so young!), Geena Davis, teenage idol Winona Ryder, and of course, Michael Keaton, playing the utterly unpredictable title character. After perishing in a car accident, Barbara (Davis) and Adam (Baldwin) find themselves stuck in their country home, unable to leave as it is invaded by the insufferable Deetze family. When Barbara and Adam are unable to frighten the Deetzes away, they call on the notorious Beetlejuice (Keaton) for help. It's a decision they live (?) to regret.

movies.title: Bell, Book And Candle
movies.description: A modern-day witch (Novak), charmed by her handsome upstairs neighbor (Stewart), casts a love spell to guarantee his infatuation. But when unexpected feelings emerge, the two neighbors find themselves united by not only the witch’s otherworldly abilities, but also by a power of this world: love. Featuring cinematography from James Wong Howe, this supernatural screwball comedy flits through frosty images of Greenwich Village in a riotous, surprisingly New York-coded reunion of two of the ‘50s most dynamic icons.

movies.title: Beloved
movies.description: Based on Toni Morrison’s 1987 novel of the same name, Demme’s Gothic horror take on one of contemporary literature’s most enduring stories is teeming with the notes that made its original text so moving: emotional, powerful, and haunting. The tale of a formerly enslaved woman plagued by a poltergeist and fantastically revisited by a reincarnated daughter, Beloved marries magical realism with the material tragedy of America’s past.

movies.title: Berlin Express
movies.description: In the aftermath of World War II, a diverse group of train passengers band together in search of a kidnapped German peace activist. One of the only American-made “rubble films” (shot in bombed-down locations across Frankfurt and Berlin), Tourneur presents a striking image of Europe after the war. It also conveys a Pynchonian flair in its constant shifting of loyalties and geographies, akin to Gravity’s Rainbow .

movies.title: Best In Show + Every Dog Has His Day: Ilak’S Birthday
movies.description: Best in Show (2000) Dir. Christopher Guest With Jennifer Coolidge, Christopher Guest, John Michael Higgins, Michael Hitchcock, Eugene Levy, Jane Lynch, Michael McKean, Catherine O'Hara, Parker Posey 89min; DCP Excitement, nerves, whining, and panting bubble up in anticipation of the Mayflower Dog Show, as a cast of eccentric dog-owners traverse the nation for the biggest day of the year. From the warbled southern drawl of Christopher Guest as Harlan Pepper to Catherine O’Hara’s unforgettable physical comedy, Parker Posey’s serious-as-a-knife portrayal of a 2000s yuppie, Jennifer Coolidge as a charmingly vapid gold-digger, and the late, great Fred Willard as a dog show judge who seemingly has never crossed paths with a dog, each performance in Best in Show is turned up to 11. Featuring arguably the funniest dog reaction shot in cinema history in its first five minutes, this largely improvised comedy is the kind of film that does not just suggest but demands repeated viewings. Christopher Guest ( Waiting for Guffman , A Mighty Wind ) is at his directorial best, amplified by a who’s who of actors extracting gut-busting performances through off-the-cuff delivery and unimaginable line reads. Preceded by: Every Dog Has His Day: Ilak’s Birthday (1925) With Ilak the Wolf Dog, Rin-Tin-Tin, Peter the Great 2min; Digital Canine actors celebrate Ilak the Wolf Dog’s birthday in this early example of dogs on the silver screen.

movies.title: Bicycle Thieves
movies.description: Hailed around the world as one of the greatest movies ever made, the Academy Award–winning Bicycle Thieves , directed by Vittorio De Sica, defined an era in cinema. In poverty-stricken postwar Rome, a desperate man is on the first day of a new job when his bicycle, which he needs for his work, is stolen. With his young son in tow, he sets off to track down the thief. Simple in construction and profoundly rich in human insight, Bicycle Thieves embodies the greatest strengths of the Italian neorealist movement: emotional clarity, social rectitude, and brutal honesty.

movies.title: Big Girls Don'T Cry
movies.cast: Ani Palmer, Rain Spencer, Noah Taylor
movies.description: 14-year-old Sid finds herself caught between her own burgeoning sexual curiosity and the desire for acceptance from an older group of girls. As she delves deeper into rebellion, she leaves behind a trail of destruction, navigating the complexities of adolescence and self-discovery.

movies.title: Bitter Christmas
movies.cast: Barbara Lennie, Leonardo Sbaraglia, Aitana Sanchez-Gijon
movies.description:
BITTER CHRISTMAS tells two alternating stories, one starring Elsa, an advertising director, in 2004, during a long weekend in December. The second takes place in 2026 and stars Raúl, a screenwriter and director who is writing a script that we soon discover is the story of Elsa, her boyfriend Bonifacio, and her friends Patricia and Natalia. Mixed with fiction, Elsa is, in a way, Raúl's alter ego, who, like him, resorts to autofiction as a solution to a long period of creative drought. He looks inside himself, and he can't help but also look at the people who make up his most intimate universe: his partner and his assistant.


The film narrates the close relationship between reality and fiction, between inspiration and life, exploring the limits of autofiction and stories within stories.

movies.title: Bitter Christmas
movies.cast: Barbara Lennie, Leonardo Sbaraglia, Aitana Sanchez-Gijon
movies.description:
BITTER CHRISTMAS tells two alternating stories, one starring Elsa, an advertising director, in 2004, during a long weekend in December. The second takes place in 2026 and stars Raúl, a screenwriter and director who is writing a script that we soon discover is the story of Elsa, her boyfriend Bonifacio, and her friends Patricia and Natalia. Mixed with fiction, Elsa is, in a way, Raúl's alter ego, who, like him, resorts to autofiction as a solution to a long period of creative drought. He looks inside himself, and he can't help but also look at the people who make up his most intimate universe: his partner and his assistant.


The film narrates the close relationship between reality and fiction, between inspiration and life, exploring the limits of autofiction and stories within stories.

movies.title: Black Cops, Spies And Overseers
movies.description: Programmed by Steven W. Thrasher and Jesse Trussell The silver screen is replete with Black cops who make us laugh (Eddie Murphy’s Axel Foley in Beverly Hills Cop , OJ Simpson’s Officer Nordberg in The Naked Gun , Cleavon Little's Bart in Blazing Saddles) and Black spies who question the American empire (Tamara Dobson in Cleopatra Jones , Lawrence Cook in The Spook Who Sat by the Doo r). Are these films “only a movie” or “just funny”—or are they policing the boundaries of our imaginations? Inspired by Steven W. Thrasher’s book The Overseer Class , this series of 12 American films made over 70 years challenges our assumptions about the performance of dramatic Black police (Sidney Poitier in In the Heat of the Night , Denzel Washington in Training Day ), outright overseers (Samuel L. Jackson in Django Unchained , Poitier in Band of Angels ), and even queerbaiting undercover spies (Al Pacino in Cruising ).

movies.title: Black Cuba
movies.description: Programmed by Yasmina Price As a cultural and political instrument, cinema was central to the Cuban Revolution, and served as a way for Afro-Cubans to assert their place in the process of collective transformation. Working across documentary, narrative, and experimental forms, the filmmakers of this watershed historical era celebrated Afro-Cuban cultural life while confronting the island’s legacies of enslavement, colonization, and ongoing racialized disparities. Black Cuba centrally showcases films from the 60s and 70s revolutionary period alongside innovative contemporary works to capture the express richness and variety of Afro-Cuban national and diasporic experiences.

movies.title: Black Girl
movies.description: Seventeen-year-old dreamer Billie Jean (Peggy Pettit) is the youngest in a family of loving yet discouraging women. Her mother, Mama Rosie (Louise Stubbs), cares deeply about her three biological children. However, her own personal disappointments have left her embittered, and she only offers encouragement to her adopted daughter, Netta (Leslie Uggams). When Netta, a successful teacher, returns to visit the family, she may be the voice of guidance and hope Billie Jean desperately needs. Followed by a Q&A with writer J.E. Franklin

movies.title: Black Girl + Borom Sarret
movies.description: Black Girl (1966) Dir. Ousmane Sembène With Mbissine Thérèse Diop 59min; DCP In French with English subtitles Father of African cinema Ousmane Sembène’s feature debut is one of the most acclaimed films ever made. Senegalese housemaid Diouana (Diop) is brought to France by the white family she works for, finding herself isolated in an unfamiliar country and trapped in a life of domestic servitude–a situation that the dignified young woman refuses to accept. Both a landmark of world cinema and a devastating indictment of colonialism’s tragic legacy, Black Girl is the first African film to receive international acclaim; Martin Scorsese called it: “an astonishing movie—so ferocious, so haunting, and so unlike anything we’d ever seen.” Sembène’s luminous black and white images have a direct expressive power, and they gleam anew in this restoration. Borom Sarret (1963) Dir. Ousmane Sembène 20min; DCP In French with English subtitles. Sembène’s first film, a neorealist look at the hardscrabble life of a wagon driver who encounters a cross-section of Dakar’s inhabitants as he makes his rounds through the streets of the city.

movies.title: Black Orpheus
movies.description: Winner of both the Academy Award for best foreign-language film and the Cannes Film Festival’s Palme d’Or, Marcel Camus’ Black Orpheus (Orfeu negro) brings the ancient Greek myth of Orpheus and Eurydice to the 20th-century madness of Carnival in Rio de Janeiro. With its eye-popping photography and ravishing, epochal soundtrack, Black Orpheus was an international cultural event, and kicked off the bossa nova craze that set hi-fis ablaze around the world.

movies.title: Black& Loving: The Artist Way
movies.description: Chronicles of a Lying Spirit (by Kelly Gabron) (1992) dir. Cauleen Smith 6min; digital Looking for "Looking for Langston" (2019) dir. Ada M. Patterson 15min; DCP Looking for Langston (1989) dir. Isaac Julien 45 min; DCP black& loving, a film program created by Tyler Green and Sokhna Samb to celebrate Black and queer artists, returns to BAM with the artist way , commemorating creators whose works have defined American culture and influenced today’s Black artists. Chronicles of a Lying Spirit (by Kelly Gabron) , directed by Cauleen Smith, offers an experimental reintegration of Black women into history. Looking for "Looking for Langston" was made by Ada M. Patterson after learning about, but being unable to see, the classic Isaac Julien work. Finally Julien’s critically acclaimed Looking for Langston explores the personal life of the beloved poet and activist Langston Hughes, incorporating archival footage from the Harlem Renaissance. These filmmakers situate their works to address the Black experience through the lens of gender and sexuality, as well as issues arising from that intersection.

movies.title: Blade Runner: The Final Cut
movies.description: While so many special effects spectacles are lost in time like tears in the rain, Blade Runner remains the template for imagining the neon-wreathed downer of the future, every bit as influential in its vision as was Fritz Lang’s Metropolis over a half…

movies.title: Blknws: Terms & Conditions
movies.description: Visual artist and filmmaker Kahlil Joseph’s video installation “BLKNWS” debuted in galleries and museums across the country in 2019, immersing viewers in the imagined world of a television news network from a Black perspective. After expanding this concept into a short film, Joseph has developed it even further into a feature film, and the result is a celebration of Black life that reconceptualizes and remediates common, corporate notions of journalism. Joseph’s sprawling film is an uninterrupted gush of ideas, mixing newly shot footage and extant media, leaping from fantastical images to historical narratives, collapsing boundaries that often separate documentary and fiction. A multidimensional work of vision and ambition, BLKNWS: Terms & Conditions offers an alternately riotous and meditative compendium of the Black experience.

movies.title: Blood Theatre
movies.description: Cooked inside a popcorn machine, stabbed in the ticket booth, fried by a film projector: these are just a few of the fates awaiting some supremely unlucky cinema workers in Rick Sloane’s bloody 1980s slasher comedy. Come out for an evening of grisly on-screen fun—and rest assured that, unlike the theater depicted on screen, you’ll be safe and sound at BAM. Featuring a reading by A.T. Pratt before the screening on February 13 .

movies.title: Blue Heron
movies.description: In the late 1990s, eight-year-old Sasha and her Hungarian immigrant family relocate to a new home on Vancouver Island, but their fresh start is interrupted by increasingly dangerous behavior from the eldest son, Jeremy. At wit’s end, their parents are presented with a shattering choice. Award-winning director Sophy Romvari’s semi-autobiographical debut feature is a lyrical, profound testament to the things we carry with us, masterfully chronicling the haze of a languid summer and the clarity of the moments that defined it. Q&A with director Sophy Romvari following the 4/21, 7pm screening

movies.title: Blue Velvet
movies.description:
David Lynch cemented his reputation as an uncompromising visionary with BLUE VELVET, one of the most controversial films of the 1980s, burrowing beneath the surface of idyllic suburban America to reveal a sinister underworld of sex and violence. After stumbling upon a severed human ear, a young college student (Kyle MacLachlan) becomes obsessed with investigating its origins and gets entangled with a nightclub chanteuse (Isabella Rossellini) and her psychopathic lover (Dennis Hopper). A masterfully eerie, depraved psychosexual nightmare and one of the greatest films of the 1980s.
“Frank Booth is the role Dennis Hopper was born and chemically mutated to own. Sometimes David Lynch can teeter too far into the absurdity for absurdity's sake, but BLUE VELVET remains perfectly balanced as it dives into the dark, bizarre underbelly of society that lurks just below the surface of suburbia. It is also worth noting that BLUE VELVET, when screened in the first month of operation at the original Alamo, was the movie that inspired our strict no-talking policy.” (Tim League, Alamo Drafthouse founder)

movies.title: Body And Soul
movies.description: Pioneering African American filmmaker Oscar Micheaux's Body and Soul , produced outside of the Hollywood system, follows an escaped convict seeking refuge by attempting to pass himself off as a reverend in a small Georgia town. In a magnetic film debut, Paul Robeson portrays two roles, the Reverend and his estranged identical twin brother. Juxtaposing the devious faux religious man against a kind young brother, Robeson’s masterful screen turn marked the beginning of what would become a legendary career in film, stage, and music.

movies.title: Body Double
movies.description: Struggling actor and claustrophobe Jake Scully becomes entranced by a mysterious neighbor’s nightly striptease, until one evening he witnesses her murder. As curiosity crosses the line into obsession, Jake chases a killer through the dark underbelly of 1980s Hollywood. In Body Double , De Palma reckons with frequent critical perception of his work as exploitative or voyeuristic, investigating the psychological underpinnings of masculine impotence and desire. Cinematographer Stephen H. Burum creates a number of disorienting magic tricks to reflect Jake’s descent into the deep—including a famous five-minute tracking shot through a Los Angeles shopping plaza. Fantasy and reality do not just co-exist, but grind against one another until they melt into one stunningly nightmarish pool of Rear Window -tinted neon sleaze.

movies.title: Born In Flames
movies.description: Set 10 years after a revolution that supposedly transformed the country into a social-democratic utopia, Lizzie Borden’s prescient postpunk provocation features a band of radicals—led by Black, lesbian, and working-class women—who fight back in a world where racism, sexism, and inequality are still the norm. Delivering a mix of TV newscasts, pirate-radio transmissions, and street-protest footage, Born in Flames conveys the incandescent rage of time when it was made, while also uncannily predicting the fragility and fragmentation of progressive movements to come.

movies.title: Bouchra
movies.description: Deeply felt, surprisingly sexy, and formally adventurous, the feature debut from acclaimed visual artists Meriem Bennani and Orian Barki (best known together from their 2020 web series 2 Lizards ) forges new ground that “will make it a classic of queer cinema for years to come” ( Next Best Picture ). With a lived-in granularity and unmistakable visual style, Bouchra is a singular portrait effortlessly toeing the line between documentary, visual art, and resonant family drama. Wrestling with writer’s block for her first film, Bouchra, a queer Moroccan jackal living in NYC starts having difficult yet overdue phone calls with her mother in Casablanca. Balancing the precarity of working as an artist in the city, the rift in her identity between her two homes, and an array of friendships and romantic interests, Bouchra’s emotional reckoning with her mother and herself becomes her path to expression.

movies.title: Bram Stoker's Dracula
movies.description: Coppola at his most boldly baroque, Gary Oldman wearing cinema’s most iconic updo, a puppyish young Keanu Reeves trying to make his way back to Winona Ryder, and Anthony Hopkins as vampire hunter Abraham Van Helsing—it’s all here in this opulent…

movies.title: Bread Day preceded by The Train Stop
movies.description: Introduction by Genevieve Yue on Saturday, September 5th

movies.title: Brief Encounter
movies.description: Introduction by Genevieve Yue on Saturday, October10th

movies.title: Broadcast News
movies.description: Introduction by Michael Barbaro of "The Daily" on Saturday, October 17th

movies.title: Buddy (2026)
movies.description: Remember Buddy, the bright orange unicorn and star of that classic children's television show who brought joy and life lessons into your living room?Inside the colorful world of "It's Buddy!", a group of children spend their days singing, dancing, and helping Buddy spread happiness. But when one child refuses to play along, Buddy is not pleased, and cracks begin to appear in this seemingly perfect world.

movies.title: Burn After Reading
movies.description: A bumbling national security state, where blackly humorous incompetence doesn’t diminish a capacity for extreme violence, is parodied in this late Bush-era satire by Joel and Ethan Coen. Burn After Reading follows recently jobless CIA analyst Osborne Cox (John Malkovich), whose misplaced memoirs are found by gym employees Linda and Chad (Frances McDormand and Brad Pitt) who mistake them for classified government documents and attempt to make a profit. Things predictably go awry in this absurd send-up of US spy culture, also starring George Clooney and Tilda Swinton. “For dark laughs and hurtling narrative momentum this spy caper is their best work since Fargo ,” the Chicago Reader proclaimed.

movies.title: Calle Málaga
movies.description: Maria Angeles, a 79 year-old Spanish woman, lives alone in Tangier, Morocco enjoying her daily routine. But her life is turned upside down when her daughter arrives from Madrid to sell the apartment she has always called home. Determined to stay, she does everything she can to get her apartment and belongings back and, unexpectedly, rediscovers love and sensuality along the way.

movies.title: Candyman
movies.description: This quintessential ‘90s fixture of contemporary horror follows a Chicago graduate student who, in the midst of studying urban folklore, accidentally summons a hook-handed ghost who appears whenever his name is chanted 5 times in front of the mirror. While the film’s campy horror thrills inspired a bevy of sequels, the original displays a heftier moral timbre: exploring the legacy of slavery in the US through the lingering story of the Candyman’s initial demise.

movies.title: Caribbean Film Series
movies.description: Programmed by Third Horizon and The Luminal Theater Our biannual series, produced in partnership with The Luminal Theater and Third Horizon, returns for a weekend of diverse original cinema created by the brightest Caribbean filmmakers. The winter lineup features new work by artists from across the Caribbean and throughout the diaspora, including local creators.

movies.title: Casino Royale (2006)
movies.description:
CASINO ROYALE (2006) takes Bond back to his origins in an unusual black-and-white foreword that hints at how the British agent earned his license to kill. The film is set in 2006, and it's risky to ask audiences to erase nearly 45 years worth of memories of a well-known character, but it's also fascinating to see the filmmakers wipe the slate clean and start again from the beginning.
Secondly, the film introduces Daniel Craig (the engaging anti-hero of the underrated crime drama LAYER CAKE) as a Bond who is still in the process of learning how to do his job, much to the consternation of his boss, M, played once again with exactly the right amount of dry humor by Judi Dench.
As interpreted by Craig, Bond is more energetic than he is suave and much more of a fighter than he is a lover. He makes some mistakes, he gets temperamental, he shows signs of vulnerability, and – best of all – he's not made of Teflon: when this Bond gets into trouble, he usually comes out with blood on his tuxedo and nasty-looking scratches on his face.
To the delight of Bond fans everywhere, CASINO ROYALE reinvigorated the series and broke the bank at the box office.

movies.title: Cat People
movies.description: Irena Dubrovna, a Serbian-born fashion illustrator, lives her New York City life under the shadow of a secret: a steadfast belief (and fear) that an ancient curse will render her a terrifying feline predator if she engages in physical intimacy. When she suspects her husband’s infidelity, she taps into her catlike instinct, stalking the alleged mistress. Eschewing the canned effects of earlier monster movies in favor of subtle shadowplay and creative audio cues, Tourneur’s noir investigation of the taboo spurred a frenzy upon its release—and elevated the stature of the horror genre.

movies.title: Caught By The Tides
movies.description: Composed of footage shot over 22 years, Jia Zhang-ke’s Caught by the Tides is a stylistic departure for the filmmaker, invoking impressionistic vignettes and a non-linear melding of fiction and reality. A working class woman (Zhao Tao) sets out to find her lover of years past, after time and circumstance thrust them apart. Moody and unsentimental, the experimental romance serves as dedication to the passage of time, and exploration of how it ebbs and flows with love.

movies.title: Change Of Life
movies.description: Co-written by Reis, Rocha’s Change of Life represents another node in the evolution of the former’s docudrama style. When Adelino returns from service in the Angolan War of Independence, he finds the woman he loves married to his brother. He skips town to find work in rural Portugal, only to find himself thrust into a surprising romance that challenges him to change his life. Though more formally traditional than his later work, Reis’ collaboration with Rocha maintains one of the key facets of his entire oeuvre: a deep commitment to portraying the complex humanity of his subjects.

movies.title: Chronovisor
movies.description: While writing a monograph on historical theories of memory, Béatrice, a respected academic, becomes beguiled by the allegedly true story of the Chronovisor, an occult device said to reproduce visuals from any point in history on a TV screen. Her obsession with the mysterious machine drags her from her Upper East Side apartment through the depths of New York City’s hidden libraries, to the edge of a breakthrough.

movies.title: Chungking Express
movies.description: A hot-shot to the heart, pop masterpiece Chungking Express tells the stories of two lovelorn cops (Takeshi Kaneshiro and Tony Leung) and the women who baffle them (Brigitte Lin and Faye Wong, who contributes a Cantopop cover of The Cranberries’…

movies.title: Cinema Paradiso
movies.description: Often credited with reviving Italy’s film industry in the late 1980s, this Oscar-winning film tells the story of a mischievous and precocious boy, Totò, who falls in love with the movies, spending every spare moment hanging around the titular theater in his small Sicilian town. When the cinema is rebuilt after a devastating fire that leaves the projectionist, Totò’s mentor, permanently blind, Totò, still a child, is tapped to run the reels, and a cinematic life suddenly unfurls before him.

movies.title: Cinema Tropical At 25: Nostalgia For The Light
movies.description: In his stirring 2010 visual essay, Chilean master documentarian Patricio Guzmán turns to the remote, high-altitude Atacama Desert to craft a meditation on memory, history, and eternity. Beneath some of the clearest skies on Earth, astronomers gather to study the origins of the universe. Yet the desert also preserves traces of the past—from pre-Columbian mummies to the remains of political prisoners disappeared after Chile’s 1973 military coup. In this otherworldly landscape, earthly and celestial quests converge: archaeologists uncover ancient civilizations, women search for their missing loved ones, and astronomers scan the heavens for distant galaxies. Nostalgia for the Light opens Guzmán’s celebrated trilogy exploring landscape, memory, and Chile’s unresolved past. Cinema Tropical continues the celebration of its 25th anniversary with landmark Latin American films of the new millennium.

movies.title: Cinema Tropical At 25: Silvia Prieto
movies.description: On her 27th birthday, Silvia Prieto decides to change her life only to spiral into an identity crisis when she discovers other women share her name. Buoyed by quick wit and a pop-infused eye for consumer culture, Silvia embarks on a wry, screwball-inspired quest for self-definition. This hilariously absurd deadpan comedy, written and directed by Latin American cinema trailblazer Martín Rejtman, became a landmark of New Argentine Cinema, inspiring a wave of filmmakers with its signature minimalism. To celebrate Cinema Tropical’s 25th anniversary, Silvia Prieto —the very first film screened by the organization—returns to New York, this time in dazzling 4K.

movies.title: Cinéma Du Cashiers
movies.description: Programmed in collaboration with film zine Cashiers Du Cinéma , this 10-film series contemplates “cinema work” itself in works of cinema—the lives and mundane thrills of those very ticket takers, popcorn scoopers, and clean-up crews who keep the fire burning within the walls of movie theaters around the world. A word from zine editors and series programmers Dan Welch and David Cardoza: “The movie theater employee has a rich psychological profile for the film-going community to readily dive into. Cashiers Du Cinéma is a showcase of this very life: a magazine by cinema workers. It’s an ode to the movies they love, to the customers they love to hate, and to the slacker code of conduct. To go along with our zine, we present to you a slew of movies which embody the ethos and popcorn-slingin’ pride that working at the movies is all about.” Zines will be available for sale; live readings to precede some screenings

movies.title: City Of Jade
movies.description: A follow up to his documentary Jade Miners , which followed those in the jade mines of Kachin State, Myanmar, City of Jade sees Midi Z turning his camera toward something more personal: his brother, a foreman at the Hpakant jade mine in Kachin State. This unflinching portrayal of the ramifications of back-breaking labor is a moving vision of documentary film-making, thrusting its viewer into the position of a man helpless to relieve his afflicted family.

movies.title: CLOWNSPIRACY
movies.description: A small town high school misfit investigates the appearance of creepy clowns before an upcoming election, discovering the clowns are more than they appear. Tickets:https://www.eventbrite.com/e/clownspiracy-tickets-1990612090348?aff=oddtdtcreator

movies.title: Club Kid
movies.cast: Jordan Firstman, Cara Delvingne, Diego Calva, Kirby Howell-Baptiste, Reggie Absolom, Colleen Camp
movies.description: Washed-up thirtysomething New York scenester Peter (Jordan Firstman), awakening from a decade-long hangover, receives an unexpected visitor: the 10-year-old British son (Reggie Absolom) he never knew he had. The result of a lone, long-forgotten sexual encounter with a woman, the kid is in desperate need of care after his mother’s death, and though Peter has never put his heart into anything other than promoting massive parties, the experience of becoming an insta-dad prompts a reconsideration of his hedonistic, drug-fueled party boy lifestyle. Swerving from irreverent satire to genuine pathos, this wildly funny and remarkably assured feature debut from writer-director-actor Firstman is an unusual and satisfying take on the challenges and pleasures of queer millennial living, and a loving reminder that it’s never too late to come of age. An A24 release.

movies.title: Coming Home
movies.description: One of the most compelling pictures ever made about the shattering aftermath of the Vietnam War, Coming Home earned eight Academy Award nominations and won three for Best Actress (Jane Fonda), Actor (Jon Voight) and Original Screenplay. Coming Home is a heartrending and unforgettable examination of a critical period in our nation's history and an uncompromising, extraordinarily moving film directed by the great Hal Ashby ( The Last Detail ). When Marine Captain Bob Hyde (Dern) leaves for Vietnam, his wife Sally (Fonda) volunteers at a local hospital. There she meets Luke Martin (Voight), a former sergeant whose war injury has left him a paraplegic. Embittered with rage and filled with frustration, Luke finds new hope and confidence through his growing intimacy with Sally. The relationship transforms Sally's feelings about life, love, and the horrors of war. And when, wounded and disillusioned, Sally's husband returns home, all three must grapple with the full impact of a brutal distant war that has changed their lives forever.

movies.title: Coming To America
movies.description: Coming to America casts comedian Eddie Murphy as pampered African prince Akeem, who rebels against an arranged marriage and heads to America to find a new bride. Murphy's regal father (Jones) allows the prince 40 days to roam the US, sending along faithful retainer Semmi (Hall) to make sure nothing untoward happens. To avoid fortune hunters, they conceal their true identity and pass as poor foreign students working at McDowell's. Akeem finds a perfect match in the boss’s daughter, Lisa (who makes a memorable dash through the rain into the subway - with Hoyt-Schermerhorn doubling for Sutphin in Queens). Murphy and Hall play multiple roles, and innumerable celebrity cameos are peppered throughout the proceedings—including the Duke Brothers from Murphy’s 1983 hit, Trading Places .

movies.title: Contemporary Arab Cinema
movies.description: This series is a labor of love—born from a simple, urgent belief that Arab filmmakers must be the ones telling our own stories. In a moment when so much feels misread or misunderstood, these films insist on being heard in their own voice. They don’t try to explain the region as much as invite you to feel its contradictions and its quiet resilience. This year’s selection—marking the series’ 14th year and 7th at BAM—travels from Morocco to Lebanon, Egypt to Saudi Arabia, Palestine to Iraq, moving between the intimate and the expansive, the fragile and the defiant. Together, they offer something rare: a space where we can see ourselves, and be seen, on our own terms. —Series programmer Lina Matta Co-presented with the Jacob Burns Film Center

movies.title: Cotton Queen
movies.description: In a cotton-farming village in Sudan, teenage Nafisa is raised on heroic tales of battling British colonizers told by her grandmother, the village matriarch Al-Sit. But when a young businessman arrives from abroad with a new development plan and genetically engineered cotton, Nafisa becomes the center of a power play to determine the future of the village. Awakening to her own strength, Nafisa sets out to save the cotton fields—and herself. Neither she nor her community will ever be the same again.

movies.title: Cotton Queen
movies.description: New York Premiere In a cotton-farming village in Sudan, teenage Nafisa is raised on heroic tales of battling British colonizers told by her grandmother, the village matriarch Al-Sit. But when a young businessman arrives from abroad with a new development plan and genetically engineered cotton, Nafisa becomes the center of a power play to determine the future of the village. Awakening to her own strength, Nafisa sets out to save the cotton fields—and herself. Neither she nor her community will ever be the same again. Followed by a Q&A with director Suzannah Mirghani, actor Rodney Sharkey, and musician Alsarah—moderated by Sarra Idris

movies.title: Coyote Vs Acme
movies.description: After countless ACME Corporation products backfire on Wile E. Coyote in his never-ending quest to vanquish the Road Runner, the despondent canine hires lawyer Kevin Avery (Forte) to sue the nefarious company. When the down-and-out attorney and Coyote realize they’ll be squaring off against the former’s ex-boss (Cena) in the case, it lights a fire under the duo—launching an unlikely friendship. The equally endearing and gut-busting adventure finally arrives in theaters after being shelved in 2023, giving Looney Tunes fans an opportunity to experience the whimsy of some of cinema’s most iconic cartoon stars back on the silver screen.

movies.title: Coyote vs. ACME
movies.description: After all of the products made by ACME Corporation backfire on Wile E. Coyote, in his pursuit of the Road Runner, he hires an equally unlucky human attorney to sue the company.

movies.title: Crocodile Dundee Ii
movies.description: Yes, we really are screening a 35mm print of Crocodile Dundee II . Mick Dundee’s (Hogan) return to the screen sets up another slew of fish-out-of-water antics in the big city. Rehashing a lot of what made the first film pop—for better or worse—Dundee’s return serves as a surprising love letter to New York City, and features a pretty iconic set piece in the Hoyt-Schermerhorn station.

movies.title: Cría Cuervos
movies.description: Taking its title from the Spanish proverb “Raise ravens and they will pick your eyes out,” Saura’s lauded allegorical masterwork, set during the twilight of Spain’s Franco dictatorship, stars Ana Torrent (also seen in Spirit of the Beehive, in the…

movies.title: Cuba & Haiti
movies.description: Three short films explore the interconnections of Cuba and Haiti in the larger narrative of the Black Caribbean. De bateyes (1971) Dir. Sara Gómez 24min, DCP Foregrounding Haitians and Afro-Cubans, this short documentary on the titular sugar mills of Cuba looks at the everyday life of its workers in a cinematic history of agriculture, labor and class struggle. Reshipment / Reembarque (2014) Dir. Gloria Rolando 58min In the early 20th century, Haitians crossed the Gulf of Gonaives to work as laborers in the cane fields. When the sugar market crashed, many were forcibly returned to Haiti. Here, the voices of prominent historians join the memories of Haitians and their descendants in Cuba to understand a complex economic chapter. Simparele (1974) Dir. Humberto Solás 30min Humberto Solas reconstructs Haitian history through music, dance, visual art, and documentary footage.

movies.title: CULT CINEMA
movies.description: Film Noir Cinema presents “CULT CINEMA”: a night of sheer cinematic madness dedicated to the most obscure films ever made.

movies.title: Dakan
movies.description: Touted as the first queer love story from West Africa, this poignant, unapologetic drama endures beyond the controversy and celebration it received upon its premiere at the 1997 Cannes Film Festival. Sory (Aboucar Touré) and Manga (Mamady Mory Camara) feel an irrepressible romantic connection they cannot deny. But after the young men share their authentic feelings with their parents, they are separated and sent in different directions. Sory begins to work in his father’s business, while Manga must spend a year with a traditional healer in the backcountry—and both are firmly encouraged to settle down with women. As Sory and Manga attempt to meet social conventions, it gradually becomes clear that their personal journeys are more parallel than divergent. A rarely screened milestone in queer cinema, Mohamed Camara’s Dakan (Destiny) is a powerful call to listen to—and trust in—one’s heart.

movies.title: Danton
movies.director: Andrzej Wajda Written by Jean-Claude Carrière, Wajda, Agnieszka Holland
movies.cast: Gérard Depardieu, Wojciech Pszoniak, Anne Alvaro

movies.title: Dao
movies.description: In his most sprawling and ambitious film to date, French Senegalese filmmaker Alain Gomis ( Félicité , NYFF55) has crafted a remarkable cinematic experience, an immersion into the rituals of one extended family, set across two continents. Dao plunges headfirst into two separate yet intrinsically interconnected ceremonies—a memorial in Guinea-Bissau and a wedding in Paris—which Gomis cuts between with kinetic abandon. Both are attended by the taciturn yet soulful middle-aged Gloria (Katy Correa), whose father has recently died and whose daughter, Nour (D’Johé Kouadio), is about to be married. Reaching ecstatic highs while also remaining grounded in the pragmatic details of the celebrations it depicts, Dao illustrates the power and persistence of African diaspora traditions. Cast with both professional actors and amateur performers, including members of the director’s own family, Gomis’s epic unfolds as a tapestry being woven before our eyes, a constant flow of movement that delicately raises questions of ancestry and assimilation, life and death, and, in its surprising construction, fiction and documentary. A Janus Films release.
