movies.title: Invisible Adversaries
movies.description: Introduction by filmmaker Lynne Sachs on Saturday, October 3rd

movies.title: Iphigenia
movies.description: The final film of Cacoyannis’s “Greek Tragedy” trilogy, following 1962’s Electra and 1971’s The Trojan Woman, adapts Euripides’s Iphigenia in Aulis, with an exceptional Tatiana Papamoschou as the waifish, doe-eyed daughter of Agamemnon and…

movies.title: Is This Thing On?
movies.description: As their marriage quietly unravels, Alex (Arnett) faces middle age and an impending divorce, seeking new purpose in the New York comedy scene while Tess (Dern) confronts the sacrifices she made for their family—forcing them to navigate co-parenting, identity, and whether love can take a new form. Bradley Cooper writes, directs, and co-stars in this understated, affecting portrait of the challenges and opportunities of starting over in middle age.

movies.title: Island Of Lost Souls + The Island Of Dr. Moreau
movies.description: These two adaptations of H.G. Wells’ enduring 1896 novel The Island of Doctor Moreau were produced over 60 years apart. Each brings its own distinctly spicy flavor to this profoundly unhinged tale of a shipwrecked man left on the island of a mad scientist whose forced, violent experiments on living creatures great and small has created a population of grotesque human-animal hybrids. With its jungle heat, laboratories of pain, and unforgettable chorus of “beast people,” Wells’ novel and its adaptations question our binary understanding of man and beast, civilization and savagery in a bleak and haunting portrayal of genius pushed to extreme cruelty. Island of Lost Souls (1932) Dir. Erle C. Kenton With Charles Laughton, Richard Arlen, Leila Hyams, Bela Lugosi, Kathleen Burke 71min; DCP The first American adaptation of H.G. Wells’ novel (itself preceded by French and German silent films), Kenton’s full-tilt, Pre-Code interpretation of Wells’ Island of Dr. Moreau captures both the disturbing, provocative horror and affecting pathos of the novel, and is still viewed by many as the quintessential adaptation. The Island of Dr. Moreau (1996) Dirs. Richard Stanley & John Frankenheimer With Marlon Brando, Val Kilmer, David Thewlis, Fairuza Balk, Ron Perlman 95min; 35mm Released on the 100th anniversary of the novel’s initial debut, this star-studded contemporary adaptation was notoriously plagued by a litany of issues during its production. The completed film, while heavy and shambolic, also crackles with the genuine chaos that went into its creation, making it a fitting foil to its predecessor.

movies.title: It Ends
movies.description: A group of recent grads head out on a late-night drive for grub, hoping to enjoy one final hangout before their paths diverge. Instead, they accidentally turn onto an endless two-lane hellscape surrounded by untold horrors and cosmic forces beyond their understanding. Written, directed, and edited by Alexander Ullom in his directorial debut, It Ends premiered at the 2025 South by Southwest Festival, and has been praised by Variety as a “brilliant” modern retelling of Jean-Paul Sartre’s No Exit .

movies.title: Ivan
movies.description: Introduction by programmer Edo Choi on Sunday, October 18th

movies.title: Jane Fonda
movies.description: Programmed by Jesse Trussell Following her appearance on stage at BAM as part of Dear Everything , we’re highlighting actress and activist Jane Fonda with a retrospective of her many illustrious cinematic works. Since the daring New Hollywood days, Fonda’s thrilling oeuvre has upended traditional depictions of women and activism on screen. From the era-defining paranoia thriller Klute to politically engaged works like The China Syndrome (not to mention Barbarella and 9 to 5 ), Fonda’s films commented on and drove forward cultural movements ranging from feminism to the anti-Vietnam war protests. A true icon in every sense, we’re thrilled to honor her appearance on stage in the Winter/Spring 2026 season with this eight-film tribute.

movies.title: Jeanne Dielman, 23 Quai Du Commerce, 1080 Bruxelles
movies.description: A singular and uniquely influential moment in film history, Chantal Akerman’s Jeanne Dielman, 23, quai du Commerce, 1080 Bruxelles meticulously details, with a sense of impending doom, the daily routine of a middle-aged widow. In its enormous spareness, Akerman’s film seems simple, but it encompasses an entire world. Both an exacting character study and one of cinema’s most hypnotic and complete depictions of space and time, the slice-of-life narrative, composed of long takes and lingering sequences, ranked first in 2022’s Sight and Sound critic’s poll of the greatest films of all time.

movies.title: Jeepers Creepers
movies.cast: Gina Philips, Justin Long, Jonathan Breck, Patricia Belcher

movies.title: Jesus Camp
movies.description: Directed by Heidi Ewing and Rachel Grady ( The Boys of Baraka ), this revealing documentary follows three devout young Christians attending Pastor Becky Fischer’s Kids on Fire School of Ministry summer camp in Devil’s Lake, ND, where children as young as six years old are taught to become dedicated Christian soldiers in “God’s Army.” In a key portrait of the ascendant religious right culture under the born-again Christian George W. Bush, the children are schooled in how to “take back America for Christ,” and trained to become a part of the country’s political future.

movies.title: Jinpa
movies.description: Stoic truck driver Jinpa picks up a vengeful hitchhiker in the desolate Kekexili plateau, aghast when he hears the young man’s intent to avenge the murder of his father a decade prior. After they part ways, Jinpa finds himself overcome with regret, setting out to find the drifter in an attempt to end the cycle of violence. Named for the Tibetan word meaning “generosity,” Jinpa won Best Screenplay in the Horizons section at the Venice Film Festival in 2018.

movies.title: Joy Of Joys
movies.description: This exuberant yet sobering documentary from Oscar-winning director Jonathan Glazer ( The Zone of Interest , NYFF61) goes behind the scenes at Abbey Road Studios to capture the recording of the Mercury Prize-nominated HELP(2) , a 2026 charity album from War Child Records, which aids children in conflict zones around the world. To make the film, Glazer enlisted some crucial help: young schoolkids from London were equipped with their own digital cameras and encouraged to shoot the studio recordings any way they wanted. Their curiosity and creativity are paralleled in footage taken by high-spirited children in war-torn parts of the globe—Gaza, Sudan, Ukraine, Yemen—whom Glazer also supplied with cameras. The resulting film, which Glazer and regular music collaborator Mica Levi have dubbed “by children, for children,” serves as a testament to youthful openness and wonder amidst the evils of the adult world. Contributing artists from the album featured in the film include Damon Albarn, Olivia Rodrigo, Cameron Winter, Arctic Monkeys, Beth Gibbons, Fontaines D.C., and Jarvis Cocker.

movies.title: Julia
movies.description: Based on a chapter from Lillian Hellman's 1973 autobiographical work Pentimento , Zinnemann’s political drama traces the stories of two women and the intersections of their lives before and during the Nazi era. The film, a tribute to a memory of Hellman’s childhood friend Julia (Redgrave), recounts the occasion of Julia’s request that Hellmen herself (Fonda) undertake a dangerous mission in service of the fight against Naziism.

movies.title: Kaili Blues
movies.description: Chen Sheng, an ex-convict turned doctor in the rural community of Kaili, sets out for Zhenyuan to find his nephew, neglected by a careless half brother. There he encounters fragments of his past and present in a tapestry of melancholy and jubilation. In a striking directorial debut, Bi Gan examines ordinary life, extracting magnificent performances from a cast of mostly non-professional actors, including his uncle (and former gangster) Chen Yongzhong.

movies.title: Kanał
movies.cast: Teresa Iżewska, Tadeusz Janczar, Wienczysław Glinski WINNER Cannes Film Festival – Special Jury Prize, 1957

movies.title: Katyń
movies.cast: Artur Zmijewski, Maja Ostaszewska

movies.title: Kiki’S Delivery Service
movies.description: A young, overeager witch—tasked with a mandatory year of independent life—relocates to a port city with her cat, where she starts a flying courier service. The wind rustles through grass against a pale blue sky, steamed buns perspire in hot bakeries, and Kiki soars to new heights as the master of Japanese animation invokes an otherworldly protagonist to exalt the minutiae of this world’s ordinary life. Nestled amid the high-flying antics and witchy witticisms is the film’s beating heart: a meditation on the mischief of youth, the daunting summit of finding one’s purpose, and the delicious possibility offered by nascent curiosity.

movies.title: Kino Canines
movies.description: Programmed by Yasmina Tawil and Rosa Martinez In 1909, Jean, a tri-colored Scotch Collie, made her on-screen debut in a silent film produced by Vitagraph Studios right here in Brooklyn. She is often credited as the very first canine actor, and became a star in her own right, known fondly as “Jean, the Vitagraph Dog.” While most of her work has since been lost, the prognostic pup paved the way for over a century of movie dogs, now appearing on BAM screens in her honor. A proper ode to kino canines naturally includes The Wizard of Oz (with Terry the Terrier as Dorothy’s iconic sidekick Toto), Lassie (starring Howard the Collie as the titular companion), and The Thin Man (with Skippy the Wire Fox Terrier as Asta). Modern iterations of four-legged friends on screen include contemporary art house films like Kelly Reichardt’s Wendy and Lucy (starring Lucy as herself), Aki Kaurismäki’s Fallen Leaves (with Alma the dog as Chaplin in a small but heart melting role), and, fresh from Egypt, Khaled Mansour’s debut Seeking Haven for Mr. Rambo (featuring the incredibly cute and talented Mr. Rambo as himself).

movies.title: Klute
movies.cast:
Jane Fonda, 
Donald Sutherland, 
Charles Cioffi, 
Nathan George, 
Dorothy Tristan, 
Roy R. Scheider, 
Rita Gam
movies.description: In the first installment of what would eventually come to be referred to as Pakula’s "paranoia trilogy" (followed by The Parallax View and All the President's Men ), Fonda hauntingly portrays Bree Daniels, a high-priced call girl stalked by a psychopath. When she crosses paths with private eye John Klute (Sutherland), a blossoming romance thrusts Klute into the position of protector as he unravels the extent of Daniels’ predicament. Fonda won the Academy Award for Best Actress for her tour-de-force performance, cementing the eerie tone of a film that investigates surveillance and the weight of being watched.

movies.title: Kuroneko
movies.description: In feudal Japan, two women are violently murdered by soldiers during a civil war, their bodies tossed aside and pawed at by a black cat. Their deaths spur something ominous: samurai returning from the war found with their throats torn out. The governor tasks a samurai with investigating the macabre murders, leading him down a mystifying path towards the otherworldly entity responsible. Desire, grief, and vengeance collide in Kaneto Shindō’s ( Onibaba , The Naked Island ) atmospheric supernatural thriller, where the boundaries between the living and the dead begin to blur. Shot in striking black and white, Kuroneko turns its shadowy forests and moonlit interiors into an eerie world of beauty and menace.

movies.title: La Bola Negra
movies.cast: Guitarricadelafuente, Milo Quifes, Carlos González
movies.description: From Cannes-winning directors Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi — popularly known as Los Javis —LA BOLA NEGRA follows three generations of men across pivotal moments in Spanish history, bound by pain, desire, and love. Carlos (Milo Quifes) longs to belong in a fractured Spain. Sebastián (Guitarricadelafuente) finds connection across enemy lines. And Alberto (Carlos González) uncovers a long-buried family secret — one that finally gives voice to truths the past tried to erase.

movies.title: La Bola Negra In 35Mm
movies.cast: Guitarricadelafuente, Milo Quifes, Carlos González
movies.description: From Cannes-winning directors Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi — popularly known as Los Javis —LA BOLA NEGRA follows three generations of men across pivotal moments in Spanish history, bound by pain, desire, and love. Carlos (Milo Quifes) longs to belong in a fractured Spain. Sebastián (Guitarricadelafuente) finds connection across enemy lines. And Alberto (Carlos González) uncovers a long-buried family secret — one that finally gives voice to truths the past tried to erase.

movies.title: La Jetée + The Last Angel Of History
movies.description: La Jetée (1962) Dir. Chris Marker With Jean Négroni, Hélène Chatelain, Davos Hanich, Jacques Ledoux 28min; DCP In French with English subtitles The Last Angel of History (1996) Dir. John Akomfrah With George Clinton, Kodwo Eshun, Edward George, Greg Tate, Ishmael Reed 45min; Digital Two short features offer disparate visions of what the future may hold. In Chris Marker’s poetically haunting La Jetée , a stylistically revolutionary 1962 time-travel fable conveyed entirely in stills, a prisoner in post-apocalyptic Paris is sent to the past and future in search of a way to save the world. In The Last Angel of History , a 1996 hybrid documentary by Ghanaian-born British artist and writer John Akomfrah, a time-traipsing “Data Thief” conducts archeological digs in search of links between Black music, Pan-African culture, and future technology, bolstered with commentary from George Clinton, Greg Tate, Octavia E. Butler, Derrick May, and other prominent figures.

movies.title: La Raulito
movies.description: Introduction and Q&A with guest curator and filmmaker Jenni Olson moderated by filmmaker Julia Solomonoff on Sunday, October 25th

movies.title: Lady
movies.description: In the restless night of Lagos, one of the city’s few female cab drivers, Lady, survives by staying tough and focused. She dreams of escape, saving her earnings for a new life far from the chaos of this Nigerian metropolis. But when long-lost childhood friend, Pinky - now a sex worker - returns with a burst of colour and trouble, Lady is pulled reluctantly into her orbit. Soon she’s driving a crew of glamorous, reckless, fun-loving women through the underbelly of Lagos nightlife. What begins as judgement becomes unexpected sisterhood: wild, tender, and disarming. As Lady becomes entangled in their world the nights grow more dangerous, and the city presses harder against old wounds she’s never confronted. Forced to face the trauma she’s long outrun, she cracks open - learning to feel, to belong, to see herself through new eyes. When everything reaches breaking point, Lady must make a choice that will change her life’s direction forever. In that choice lies a new kind of freedom: one rooted not in escape, but in transformation. Followed by a Q&A with director Olive Nwosu, moderated by Karen McMullen

movies.title: Laila’S Birthday
movies.description: When government cuts force a judge (Mohammed Bakri) to make a career pivot, Abu Laila finds himself driving a taxi in the hectic streets of the West Bank. On the day of his daughter's birthday, his wife insists that he needs to be home early with a present and a cake. The proud ex-judge embarks on a sprawling urban odyssey plagued by gridlock, disorderly passengers, and the myriad plights affecting daily life under occupation.

movies.title: Land Of The Dead
movies.description: In the fourth installment of Romero’s legendary Dead series, the zombies have finally taken over the planet. All that’s left for humanity are isolated city-states, where the rich maintain a strict social hierarchy. Romero, who long used his zombie stories as a site of social critique, fashions the authoritarian leader Paul Kaufman (Dennis Hopper) into an explicit George W. Bush analog when he yells “I don't negotiate with terrorists!”

movies.title: Lassie +  Jean Rescues
movies.description: Lassie is shown alongside Jean Rescues , featuring America’s first canine screen star, Jean the Vitagraph Dog. Lassie (1994) Dir. Daniel Petrie With Helen Slater, Tom Guiry, Jon Tenney 94min; Digital Perhaps no pup is more synonymous with canines on screen than Lassie, the decade and medium-spanning collie. Across film and television, nine canine thespians took up the mantle of the screen’s most famous pooch, first originated in a 1938 short story by Eric Knight. Sweetly hitting all the right beats of a family romp—while backed by the sounds of The Beatles, Bob Dylan, and the Allman Brothers—the titular dog’s 1994 foray on the silver screen serves as a charming portrait of the power of a dog’s love. Preceded by: Jean Rescues (1911) Dir. Lawrence Trimble With Florence Turner, Leo Delaney, William Humphrey, Jean 12min; Digital Alice and her nit-picking fiance Oscar are at the beach alongside Jean—Alice’s dog and a constant annoyance to Oscar. When Oscar’s penchant for jealousy leaves another beachgoer in danger, the heroic Jean must save the day.

movies.title: Last Year At Marienbad
movies.description: Not just a defining work of the French New Wave but one of the great, lasting mysteries of modern art, Alain Resnais’s epochal Last Year at Marienbad (L ’année dernière à Marienbad ) has puzzled appreciative viewers for decades. Written by Alain Robbe-Grillet, a radical master of the New Novel, this surreal fever dream gorgeously fuses timelines while telling the ambiguous tale of a man and a woman (Giorgio Albertazzi and Delphine Seyrig) who may or may not have met a year ago, perhaps at the very same cathedral-like, mirror-filled château they now find themselves wandering. Unforgettable in both its haunting scope and confounding details (gilded ceilings, diabolical parlor games, a loaded gun, sudden appearances and disappearances) Resnais’s investigation into the nature of memory is disturbing, romantic, and maybe even a ghost story.

movies.title: Le Pont Du Nord
movies.description: A bank robber (Bulle Ogier) recently released from prison and a young woman (portrayed by Bulle’s daughter, Pascale) roam the streets of Paris, cinematically reimagined as a sprawling board game, in a quest to understand the contents of a mysterious suitcase. A gorgeously rendered portrait of Paris imbued with an ever-present ominous rhythm, the playful middle period work from Rivette shares with Pynchon an interest in conspiracy and secret histories.

movies.title: Leviticus
movies.description: In a conservative Australian town, the most terrifying thing facing two queer teens isn’t just the ostracization of their community, but a more sinister entity that takes the form of the person they desire most: each other. With captivating performances from its breakout stars, this striking debut from director Adrian Chiarella deftly weaves a truly haunting premise and moments of sweet romance into a larger tapestry investigating the toll of contemporary bigotry.

movies.title: Little Women
movies.description: Winona Ryder would receive an Academy Award nomination for Best Actress for her role as the headstrong, literary minded Jo March in Armstrong’s perfectly enchanting adaptation of Louisa May Alcott’s 1868 novel of the same name, about the travails of…

movies.title: Lone Star
movies.description: In the sleepy hamlet of Frontera, two off-duty cops discover a buried skeleton at an old shooting range, prompting an investigation from straight-arrow Sheriff Sam Deeds (Chris Cooper). Soon it’s revealed the body belongs to Sam’s notoriously corrupt predecessor Charlie Wade (Kris Kristofferson) and a twisty, old-fashioned murder mystery ensues, aided immensely by a killer ensemble cast (Frances McDormand, Elizabeth Peña, Joe Morton and Matthew McConaughey) and music by Mason Daring. Maybe the most celebrated film of John Sayles’ career, Lone Star disentangles Texas mythology with shrewd attention to the shifting mores and demographics of the contemporary West.

movies.title: Los Angeles Plays Itself
movies.description: Los Angeles is more than where movies are made; it also provides the thematic undercurrent for a myriad of iconic moments in cinema history. Thom Andersen's documentary Los Angeles Plays Itself explores this complicated tapestry and the ways in which the town and the works created within it interact. An avowed fan of classic Hollywood, the west coast mecca has a major place in Pynchon’s personal lore as his primary residence in the 60s and early 70s. His examination of the city’s counter culture up close in Manhattan Beach informs a lot of his west coast novels, which are comfortably in conversation with Thom Anderson’s magnum opus on Hollywood and the history of power in California.

movies.title: Los Nadie (The Nobodies)
movies.description: In Medellín, five friends on the precipice of leaving adolescence are entrenched in the unrest, rage, and tenderness of youth. Living on the outskirts of a city that excludes them, they embrace music, street art, and friendship as weapons of resistance in this coming of age ensemble film.

movies.title: Los Punks + Beyond The Screams
movies.description: From Los Angeles to Chicago, New York, Santa Fe, and more, the Latino/Chicano punk movement developed within the U.S. as a means for young people to express themselves and resist growing societal oppression. Los Punks showcases the development of this movement specifically in LA, while Beyond the Screams explores the wider development of Latino punk throughout the U.S. from the ‘70s through the early ‘90s. Los Punks: We Are All We Have (2016) Dir. Angela Boatwright 79min; Digital This intimate documentary follows teens and young adults who find meaning in the thriving punk rock scene in the backyards of South Central and East Los Angeles. Beyond the Screams (Mas Alla de Los Gritos) (1999) Dir. Martin Sorondeguy 29min; Digital In English and Spanish with English subtitles From the late 1970s up until the early 1990s, young people looking for a way to empower themselves began to develop a Latino/Chicano punk movement across the U.S. Martin Sorrondeguy, singer of hardcore punk bands Los Crudos and Limp Wrist, and a prominent figure in both the straight edge scene and the queercore scene, follows the development of the scene through the decades in major Latino cities. Composed of interviews and live performances, this film focuses on the struggle of Latino/Chicano artists against globalization, poverty, and identity.

movies.title: Lotna
movies.cast: Jerzy Pichelski, Adam Pawlikowski, Bożena Kurowska, Jerzy Moes, Mieczysław Łoza,

movies.title: Maddie’S Secret
movies.description: Inspired by Douglas Sirk, Todd Haynes, Showgirls , and the nearly pornographic world of online food influencers, comedian, writer, and actor John Early makes his critically acclaimed directorial debut with the story of a breakout new-media star who’s hiding a secret. Early portrays Maddie, a dishwasher at L.A. food-content creation studio Gourmaybe, who makes her own vegetarian cooking videos at home with help from her adoring husband (Eric Rahill). When one of her videos goes viral, Maddie is thrust into the influencer sphere herself, straining her bond with her sassy queer BFF (Kate Berlant) and threatening to expose her struggle with an eating disorder. Blending satire and melodrama, the film announces a bold new voice in contemporary cinema.

movies.title: Malcolm X
movies.description: The culmination of a longtime dream, Malcolm X exemplifies director Spike Lee’s unique vision and style, moving elegantly between genres and time periods with a dazzling array of camera movements and meticulous editing as he tells the life story of the iconic leader. Denzel Washington embodies Malcolm with conviction, force, and dignity in one of his most indelible performances.

movies.title: Maluala
movies.description: Maluala takes us into a palenque —a fortified settlement of escaped slaves—hidden in Cuba’s eastern mountains, as the Spanish colonial forces attempt to sow discord among their leaders. The film marks Giral’s third entry into his trilogy of films about slavery in 19th-century Cuba and the Caribbean, combining a Marxist lens with the long arc of Black Liberation to trace the development from individual to collective struggle.

movies.title: Man Of Iron
movies.cast: Krystyna Janda, Jerzy Radziwiłowicz, Marian Opania WINNER Cannes Film Festival – Palme d’Or, 1981

movies.title: Man Of Marble
movies.cast: Krystyna Janda, Jerzy Radziwiłowicz, Tadeusz Łomnicki,

movies.title: Marty Supreme
movies.description: Timothée Chalamet “makes one of the most colossal movie performances of the 21st century seem as natural as a lay-up” ( IndieWire ) in the latest offering from director Josh Safdie (co-director, Good Time , Uncut Gems ). Performing with a distinguished cast that includes Gwyneth Paltrow, Odessa A'zion, and Tyler Okonma (a.k.a. Tyler, the Creator), Chalamet gives “the defining performance of his still-burgeoning career” ( Variety ) as would-be ping-pong champion Marty Mauser, a young man with a dream no one respects, who goes to hell and back in pursuit of greatness.

movies.title: Mary Jane'S Not A Virgin Anymore
movies.description: When a bright, self-possessed movie theater employee decides to lose her virginity, she discovers that sex is less a rite of passage than a series of awkward negotiations. Sasha Jacobson’s ( I Was a Teenage Serial Killer ) sharply observed indie coming-of-age story charts the debauched misadventures of a slacker squad of co-workers. Keep an eye out for cameos by iconic punk frontmen Jello Biafra and Davey Havok. Featuring a reading by Josh Bayer before the screening on February 14.

movies.title: María Antonia
movies.description: New York Premiere of New Restoration This tragedy follows a rebellious woman living in an Afro-Cuban Havana neighborhood during the 1950s, and the crime of passion that arises amid her entangled love life. Followed by a Q&A with writer Armando Dorrego

movies.title: Masahiro Shinoda
movies.description: Co-presented by the Japan Foundation Programmed by Jesse Trussell The protean master filmmaker Masahiro Shinoda, who passed away last year at 94, deftly leapt between social dramas, samurai films, and stunning engagements with traditional Japanese theater. Beginning his career in the 1950s as an assistant to legends like Yasujirō Ozu ( Tokyo Story ), his early youth-oriented films (many written by the radical poet, theater-maker, and firebrand Shuji Terayama) established Shinoda as an early master of the Japanese New Wave. By the mid-to-late 60s, his work had become increasingly stylized: the icy wide-screen of Pale Flower and the Noh theater of Double Suicide . Shinoda would go on to amass a career spanning five decades and global acclaim. This series gathers 12 films from across a half-century—many in new restorations and prints imported from Japan—that reveal Shinoda as one of the supreme masters of Japanese cinema.

movies.title: Master And Commander: The Far Side Of The World
movies.description: In this saga set during the Napoleonic Wars, adapted loosely from Patrick O'Brian's Aubrey–Maturin series, a captain of the British Royal Navy (Crowe) pursues his enemy across the seas—posing questions about the interplay between duty and loyalty along the way. The Pynchon connection? The novelist names a storyteller—“the best Yarn-Spinner in all the Fleets”—after O’Brian in Mason & Dixon , his own sprawling historical adventure tale.

movies.title: May Your Eyes Be Blessed: Film And Tv Work Of Luiz Fernando Carvalho
movies.description: Programmed by Madeleine Molyneaux & Carlos Valladares Luiz Fernando Carvalho is among the most inventive visual stylists in Brazilian film and television, yet his poetic, unruly oeuvre remains largely unknown in the US. Inspired by the examples of Glauber Rocha, Marguerite Duras, Pier Paolo Pasolini, and Luchino Visconti, Carvalho has brought a bold, “contaminated” sensibility to feverish adaptations of texts by Machado de Assis, Ariano Suassuna, Graciliano Ramos, and especially Clarice Lispector, while also reinterpreting Brazil’s history, myths, and emotional and political landscapes. This series includes the North American premiere of The Passion According to G.H. , Carvalho’s award-winning treatment of Lispector’s supposedly “unfilmable” 1964 novel, plus his landmark first feature film, To the Left of the Father (Lavoura Arcaica) , and more celebrated work in cinema and television. Also screening are films personally selected by Carvalho that have fired his imagination. This overdue retrospective introduces New York audiences to a filmmaker hailed by Bernardo Bertolucci as “master of himself and of us all.” Luiz Fernando Carvalho and actress Maria Fernanda Cândido will be present for select events.

movies.title: Medea (1988)
movies.description: Based on an unfilmed screenplay by Carl Theodor Dreyer and, of course, Euripides’s tragedy of the same title, von Trier’s made-for-television film—save for two epiphanic eruptions—is uncharacteristically austere, the enfant terrible of Danish…

movies.title: Memoria
movies.description: Startled at daybreak by an inexplicable loud bang of unknown origin while visiting her sister in Colombia, Scottish botanist Jessica (Tilda Swinton) sets out to discover the source of the sound, leading to encounters with doctors, audio engineers, and archaeologists uncovering ancient human remains at a construction site. The first international production and English-language feature by Thai auteur Apichatpong Weerasethakul ( Uncle Boonmee Who Can Recall His Past Lives , Cemetery of Splendour ), Memoria is not only a bold, audacious film, but also a ringing endorsement of watching films on large screens in darkened rooms among other viewers—the only way Weerasethakul intends for this feature to be experienced.

movies.title: Memories Of Love Returned
movies.description: On April 24, 2002, filmmaker Ntare Guma Mbaho Mwine’s car broke down in the small town of Mbirizi, Uganda. While waiting for it to be repaired, he stumbled upon a small photo studio and met photographer Kibaate Aloysius Ssalongo, whose work spanned from the late 1950s to his death in 2006. This chance encounter turned into a 22-year journey documenting and exploring Kibaate’s life, photography, and the profound impact his work had on the community he documented, as well as Mwine’s own life. Followed by a Q&A with director Ntare Guma Mbaho Mwine, moderated by Delphine Fawundu

movies.title: Mermaids
movies.description: It’s 1963, and different-drummer single mother Cher has decided to move from Oklahoma to smalltown Massachusetts, uprooting her two daughters, nine-year-old Kate and Catholicism-obsessed 15-year-old Rachel (Winona Ryder, who provides the narration).…

movies.title: Midnight in Paris
movies.description: Screenwriter, would-be novelist, and romantic-at-heart Owen Wilson, on vacation in the City of Lights with level-headed fiancée Rachel McAdams, sets out on his own one night after a wine tasting and finds himself suddenly in the Jazz Age Paris of…

movies.title: Migration And Movement
movies.description: Two sensitive and speculative films chart the migratory experiences of people in the Cuban diaspora. Cuban Roots/Bronx Stories (2000) Dir. Pam Sporn 57min, digital A Black Cuban family in the Bronx experiences some of the great historical events of the 20th century intimately, yet from a distance—Castro’s arrival in Havana, the Bay of Pigs invasion, the Vietnam war—in this singular project by director Pam Sporn. Naufragio (2012) Dir. Dami Sainz Edwards 6min, digital Filmmaker Dami Sainz Edwards uses repetition and superimposition to look at the act of diving into water, evoking the migratory movement of the Cuban people. Introduced by Pam Sporn on Monday, Feb 23

movies.title: Millennium Mambo
movies.description: Shu Qi ( The Assassin ) portrays Vicky, an aimless bar hostess caught between a possessive boyfriend (Duan Chun-hao) and a sensitive gangster (Jack Kao), in this stylish, seductive submersion into the techno-scored neon nightlife of Taipei directed by Hou Hsiao-hsien—named “one of the three directors most crucial to the future of cinema” in a worldwide poll conducted by the New York Film Festival in 1998. Looking back from the then near-future of 2011, Vicky envisions her life of 10 years earlier rendered in a transfixing, narcotic haze of techno, slo-mo, and iridescent imagery, along with an inescapable undercurrent of ennui.

movies.title: Minority Report
movies.description: Based on a Philip K. Dick short story, Spielberg’s wheeling, virtuoso science-fiction thriller stars Tom Cruise as an investigator of “PreCrime” who specializes in arresting criminals before they’ve done the deed in near-future Washington, DC.…

movies.title: Minotaur
movies.cast: Dmitriy Mazurov, Iris Lebedeva, Boris Kudrin

movies.title: Miracle Mile
movies.description: Mostly portrayed in tense real-time, De Jarnatt’s apocalyptic thriller follows a young man who overhears a phone call revealing that a nuclear war has started and missiles will hit Los Angeles within 70 minutes. The bleak exploration of the moments before an impending nuclear holocaust is kept in balance by a romantic fatalism, and contains a unique explicit nod to Pynchon: an apocryphal “Cliff’s Notes for Gravity’s Rainbow .”

movies.title: Miroirs No. 3
movies.description: When piano student Laura (Beer) miraculously survives a car crash, she finds herself in the devoted care of a local woman. Her recovery becomes two-fold as she heals physically and attempts to reconnect with the world, finding a strange harmony with her new adoptive family. Acclaimed director Christian Petzold ( Phoenix , Transit ) spins a modern gothic fairytale revolving around the lies we tell ourselves and the strange ways that grief, connection, and humanity bind and sustain us.

movies.title: Mississippi Masala
movies.description: Arguably one of the sexiest movies of the ‘90s, Mira Nair’s interracial star-crossed love story is hot in every sense: swampy Southern nights and motel-room dalliances, but also explosive political violence and family tension ready to boil over at any moment. Forced to flee Uganda under dictator Idi Amin and resettle in the US, Mina’s life is turned upside down once again when she begins a passionate—and taboo—love affair with Demetrius, a Black man who shares her dream of a bigger life beyond Greenwood, Mississippi. The languorous atmosphere that hangs over the film is not just about desire, but yearning of another kind: an exile’s need for belonging. Nair’s keen awareness of both the minutiae of relationships and their much broader socio-political context gives the film a depth as key to its enduring popularity as witnessing a shorts-clad Denzel Washington at his face-melting peak.

movies.title: Mississippi Masala
movies.description: Mississippi Masala (1991) Dir. Mira Nair With Sarita Choudhury, Denzel Washington 118min; DCP Uganda, US Forced to flee Uganda after dictator Idi Amin expels Asians from the country, Mina (Sarita Choudhury) and her Indian family resettle in Mississippi, hoping to rebuild their lives. There she forms a deep connection with Demetrius (Denzel Washington), a Black local. Their relationship sparks tension as both families and their communities struggle with the racial boundaries it crosses. As hostility grows and pressure mounts, Mina and Demetrius must decide whether to remain loyal to their families or follow their love. Preceded by: Weeyagale (2025) Dir. Ainslie Senfuka With Esme Green, Edith Kaggwa, Abiah Ndagire 6min; DCP UK In English and Ganda with English subtitles A magical-realist drama follows a young British-Ugandan girl whose classroom show-and-tell unlocks a dreamlike journey into her heritage.

movies.title: Misty Green
movies.description: In the captivating, star-making performance at the center of writer/director Chris Rock’s L.A. odyssey, Rosalind Eleazar plays Misty Green, an Emmy-winning former actress now struggling to make ends meet in an unforgiving Hollywood of humiliating auditions and fair-weather friends. With seven days to move out of her dead ex-boyfriend’s house, Misty is thrust into a frantic week in which she tries to secure a job and get her life on track—no easy task in any case, but especially complicated by run-ins with a sleazy former colleague (Adam Driver), her brother (Daniel Kaluuya) who’s struggling with mental illness, and an acclaimed movie director (Rock) who might provide Misty’s path to her dream role. Rock, clearly well-versed in the city’s culture and lifestyle—as well as its blind spots and bigotries—never settles for easy solutions, as his freewheeling, deft, and ambitious drama offers genuine darkness beneath its sunny veneer. The marvelous supporting cast includes Anna Kendrick, Topher Grace, and Anthony Anderson. An A24 release.

movies.title: Misty Green
movies.description: Years after her Hollywood breakthrough, a talented actress whose career has stalled fights for her second act.

movies.title: Mix Nyc Presents Barbara Hammer Through The Eyes Of Others
movies.description: Curated by Jac Renée Bruneau The pioneering lesbian experimental filmmaker Barbara Hammer produced more than 80 films between 1968 and 2019; this program showcases an array of works that explore her artistic output, her as a being, and the ripple effects both continue to have. The filmmaker began this process herself while she was alive— Audience offers a playful array of snippets from conversations about her work with attendees of numerous screenings. The program goes on to move through films by filmmakers who were/are in conversation with Hammer—from engaging in her practices to making homages, writing letters, and (upon Hammer’s invitation) even using her footage. Audience (1982) Dir. Barbara Hammer 32min Love, Barbara (2022) Dir. Brydie O’Connor 15min Untitled (Dyketactics Revisited) (2005) Dir. Liz Rosenfeld 13min Carolee, Barbara and Guvnor (2018) Dir. Lynne Sachs 9min A Video Letter to Barbara Hammer (2018) Dir. Joey Carducci 17min A Month of Single Frames (2019) Dir. Lynne Sachs 14min Followed by a Q&A with Brydie O’Connor and Joey Carducci, moderated by Jac Renée Bruneau

movies.title: Moonlight (10Th Anniversary Remastered)
movies.cast: Trevante Rhodes, Ashton Sanders, Alex Hibbert, Mahershala Ali, Naomie Harris, Jharrel Jerome, Janelle Monáe, André Holland
movies.description: This landmark Best Picture winner returns to the big screen after a decade, newly restored in 4K and with exclusive behind-the-scenes insights from filmmaker Barry Jenkins and composer Nicholas Britell to follow the feature. A timeless story of human connection and self-discovery, MOONLIGHT chronicles the life of a young black man from childhood to adulthood as he struggles to find his place in the world while growing up in a rough neighborhood of Miami. This groundbreaking film is both a vital portrait of contemporary African American life and a deeply personal and poetic meditation on identity, family, friendship, and love.

movies.title: Moonrise
movies.description: Based on the 1946 novel of the same name, Frank Borzage’s Moonrise follows the son of a man hanged for murder, the catalyst for a life plagued by bullying and ostracization. In a particularly fraught confrontation, the young Danny (Dane Clark) kills one of his tormentors in self defense. He soon develops a fledgling relationship with the deceased man’s fiancée, a schoolteacher who finds herself increasingly charmed by the afflicted man. This postwar noir from Borzage serves as a hidden gem within the catalogue of an auteur often neglected in the chronicling of early Hollywood.

movies.title: Mother Mary
movies.description: Long-buried wounds rise to the surface when iconic pop star Mother Mary (Anne Hathaway) reunites with her estranged best friend and former costume designer Sam Anselm (Michaela Coel) on the eve of her comeback performance. Between original songs from Charli XCX, a protagonist loosely-inspired by Taylor Swift, and a cast including Hathaway, Coel, Hunter Schafer, and FKA Twigs, Lowery’s ( The Green Knight ) latest combines striking fashion with daring drama.

movies.title: Mr Arkadin
movies.description: Zipping around postwar Europe in a mystery that reveals the criminal capitalism that rose in the wake of fascism, this Orson Welles masterpiece (loved by the Cahiers du Cinéma critics) screens on 35mm in the so-called “Corinth” version, AKA Confidential Report —one of nine jumbled variations released over the years. A Pynchonian look at the liminal spaces of Italy, Spain, and Germany after WWII, it features a cast of eccentric character actors like Akim Tamiroff, Paola Mori, Michael Redgrave, and the always magnetic Welles himself.

movies.title: Mubi Notebook Presents: I Am Love
movies.description: The new issue of Notebook , MUBI’s film journal, is devoted to the art of food on film. To celebrate, BAM is thrilled to screen Luca Guadagnino’s lush melodrama I Am Love , featuring an introduction by bestselling cookbook author Alison Roman and critic Elissa Suh. In turn-of-the-millennium Milan, the wife of a wealthy industrialist (Tilda Swinton) slips into a torrid affair with a talented chef (Edoardo Gabbriellini). For these lovers, food and sensuality are one and the same. From cakes to ukha, every dish he prepares only turns up the heat between them—and an unforgettable dish of glazed prawns is their gateway to unbridled passion.

movies.title: Murmur Of Youth
movies.description: After dropping out of college and discovering the boy she likes doesn’t like her back, suburban Chen takes a job at a Taipei movie theater, where she meets Ling working in the ticket booth. Soon, a slow-simmering friendship grows between them in this sincere and irresistible Taiwanese coming-of-age film directed by Lin Cheng-sheng.

movies.title: Musk
movies.cast: Elon Musk, Justine Musk, Ashley St. Clair
movies.description: An incisive look behind the legend of Elon Musk, the world’s most heralded “inventor-entrepreneur” who has enormous influence on the world in which we all live.

movies.title: My Country, My Country
movies.description: Working alone in Iraq over eight months, filmmaker Laura Poitras ( Citizenfour , All the Beauty and the Bloodshed ) creates an extraordinarily intimate portrait of Iraqis living under US occupation. Her principal focus is Dr. Riyadh, an Iraqi medical doctor, father of six and Sunni political candidate. An outspoken critic of the occupation, he is equally passionate about the need to establish democracy in Iraq, arguing that Sunni participation in the January 2005 elections is essential. Yet all around him, Dr. Riyadh sees only chaos, as his waiting room fills each day with patients suffering the physical and mental effects of ever-increasing violence. Nominated for an Academy Award, My Country, My Country is a powerful mosaic of daily life in Iraq.

movies.title: My Father’S Shadow
movies.description: My Father’s Shadow (2025) Dir. Akinola Davies Jr. With Sopé Dìrísù 93min; DCP Nigeria, UK In English, Nigerian Pidgin, and Yoruba with English subtitles The UK’s Best International Feature Film entry to the 98th Academy Awards and recipient of the Caméra d’Or Special Mention at Cannes, Akinola Davis Jr.’s My Father’s Shadow is a poetic, tender portrait of father–son bonds. Framed by the political landscape of 1993 Lagos, the film follows a father and his two young sons as they journey into and around the vibrantly rendered Nigerian metropolis, quietly reckoning with their relationship while navigating a city on the precipice of democratic crisis. Brothers and collaborators Akinola Davies Jr. and Wale Davies bring us a groundbreaking feature debut—centering an award-winning performance by Sopé Dìrísù ( Slow Horses , Gangs of London )—that reveals the profound depths of what families leave unspoken. Followed by a Q&A with actor Sopé Dìrísù Preceded by: Lizard (2020) Dir. Akinola Davies Jr. With Pamilerin Ayodeji, Osayi Uzamere, Charles Etubiebi 18min; DCP UK, Nigeria, 18m In English and Pidgin with English subtitles After eight-year-old Juwon gets removed from bible class by her Sunday school teacher, she follows an agama lizard into the bowels of the “Heaven’s Gate Ministries” mega church. Her journey into the labyrinth exposes the financial inner workings and the hidden activities behind the scenes. Plunging her deeper until she is confronted by a spellbinding sermon and a congregation worshipping in a hypnotised frenzy. Magical interactions with an alarmingly larger lizard and a sturdy gateman serve as metaphors for the preceding incidents. As her family proceeds to leave the church, they are intercepted by the dramatic confrontation with a gang of holy armed robbers.

movies.title: My Imaginary Country + Chile’S Student Uprising
movies.description: Chile’s Student Uprising (2014) Dir. Roberto Navarrete 35min; Digital In English and Spanish with English subtitles During the nation’s mass student protests between 2011 and 2013, director Roberto Navarrete traveled to Chile to speak to student leaders like Camila Vallejo and Giorgio Jackson (both later key figures in the Gabriel Boric government) about their demands for a state-funded education system and other radical social changes. In a series of interviews, Chile’s Student Uprising unpacks why these protests had such an effect in Chile and inspired others in the country and beyond. My Imaginary Country (2022) Dir. Patricio Guzmán 83min; DCP In Spanish with English subtitles When the Social Outburst exploded in Chile in 2019, one and a half million people took to the streets of Santiago demanding justice, education, health care, and a new constitution to replace the strident rules imposed on the country during the Pinochet military dictatorship. Patricio Guzmán, a longtime documentarian of Chile’s socio-political landscape, set out to document the demonstrations that would forever alter the trajectory of his nation. Urgent and inspired, My Imaginary Country features harrowing front-line protest footage and interviews with dynamic activist leaders, powerfully connecting Chile's complex, bloody history to contemporary revolutionary social movements—and the election of a new president.

movies.title: My Undesirable Friends: Part Ii – Exile: Chapters 1-3
movies.director: Julia Loktev Executive Produced By Meryl Streep And Laura Poitras The Film Will Be Shown In Two Sections: Chapters 1-3 (192 Min
movies.description: When Russia shuts down all independent media, a group of young dissident journalists must flee Moscow so they can keep reporting and not go to prison. In her riveting follow-up to last year’s awards-sweeping MY UNDESIRABLE FRIENDS — LAST AIR IN MOSCOW, Julia Loktev follows these courageous, sharply funny women (and a few men) as they fan out across a dozen countries, to Istanbul, Tbilisi, Prague, Vienna, Amsterdam, New York, and beyond. Over the course of four years, they continue to report the

movies.title: My Wife Cries
movies.description: A withdrawn construction worker named Thomas (Vladimir Vulevic) leaves work one day to discover his wife, Carla (Agathe Bonitzer), on a park bench, tearful and distraught following an emergency. What she proceeds to reveal tests the limits of their seemingly comfortable marriage, her sudden honesty upending their perceptions about themselves and one another. This simple yet gripping set-up beckons into being a formally audacious portrait of contemporary anxieties around love, gender, and trauma, set against the beautifully forlorn countryside surrounding Berlin. Once again expertly balancing enigmatic detachment and emotional transparency, the singular German director Angela Schanelec ( Music , NYFF62) has crafted one of her finest and most unexpected relationship dramas, working against melodrama while spellbinding the viewer with its drifting inquiry into human behavior.

movies.title: Mysterious Object At Noon
movies.description: Apichatpong Weerasethakul brought an appetite for experimen­tation to Thai cinema with his debut feature, an uncategorizable work that refracts documentary impressions of his homeland through the surrealist concept of the “exquisite corpse.” Enlisting locals to contribute improvised narration to a simple tale, Weerasethakul charts the collective construction of the fiction as each new encounter imbues it with unpredictable shades of fantasy and pathos. Shot over the course of two years in black-and-white 16mm, Mysterious Object at Noon established the director’s defining fascination with the porous boundaries between the real and the imagined.

movies.title: Nadie Es Inocente (Nobody Is Innocent)
movies.description: This hybrid documentary follows “Kara,” a member of Los Mierdas Punks (The Punk Shits), as he embarks on a train journey to leave behind his life of hell-raising in Ciudad Neza. On his trip, he reflects on the scenes and stories that comprised his debaucherous life. Minter’s pivotal work combines elements of documentary and dramatization, with the young Mierdas Punks playing themselves onscreen and collaborating on the development of the film.

movies.title: Nadja
movies.description: Michael Almereyda’s ( Tesla , Experimenter , Hamlet ) 1994 work of horror—executive produced by David Lynch—centers on young vampire Nadja (Elina Löwensohn) as she attempts to reunite with her twin brother following their father’s death from a stake in the heart at the hands of Dr. Van Helsing (Peter Fonda). The cult-classic, which fuses shimmering black-and-white 35mm with the hallucinatory grain of Pixelvision video, draws inspiration from Dracula’s Daughter (1936) and André Breton’s surrealist novel Nadja . We’re thrilled to screen a brand-new 4K restoration of the director’s cut. A Grasshopper Film and Arbelos Films Release Featuring two Q&As with director Michael Almereyda, moderated on February 6 by critic Stephanie Zacharek at 7pm and on February 7 by filmmaker Azazel Jacobs at 7pm

movies.title: National Theatre Live: Dear England
movies.description: Part love letter to the beautiful game, part biographical retelling, writer James Graham’s play Dear England follows the trajectory of manager Gareth Southgate and his attempted resurrection of the historically underperforming English national football team through three pivotal tournaments: the 2018 World Cup, UEFA Euro 2020, and the 2022 World Cup. Nominated for nine Olivier awards upon its 2024 run (including Best New Play for Graham), the National Theatre’s screening of the football stage sensation arrives on BAM screens for a select engagement. Presented as part of a multi-year partnership with BAM and National Theatre. Bringing the National Theatre to New York—on stage, on screen, and in the classroom.

movies.title: Naza
movies.description: In secret conversations on the rooftops of Tel Aviv at night, the systems behind Israel’s calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza are revealed by the people who designed and operated them.

movies.title: Naza
movies.description: In secret conversations on the rooftops of Tel Aviv at night, the systems behind Israel’s calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza are revealed by the people who designed and operated them.

movies.title: Ndar, Saga Waalo
movies.description: Ndar—the original name of the Senegalese capital Saint-Louis—lies on an island at the mouth of the Senegal River in the former Waalo kingdom, and served as a key port of colonial expansion into West Africa four centuries ago. As an economic, cultural, and political crossroads, the city became a laboratory for France’s so-called “civilizing mission,” where commerce, urban planning, education, and racial mixing were used to assimilate local populations and consolidate colonial power. Today, Saint-Louis holds a complex legacy: while some residents acknowledge this history and maintain longstanding Saint-Louisian traditions, others call for a decisive break from its colonial past. For many young people in particular, the moment demands a new way of thinking about history.

movies.title: Never After Dark
movies.cast: Moeka Hoshi, Kurumi Inagaki, Kento Kaku
movies.description: A wandering medium, Airi spends her life guiding restless spirits out of the world of the living. Summoned to an isolated country house, she comes face to face with a grotesque apparition with powers that defy Airi's experience. As she digs deeper into the house's past, a secret comes to light -- and Airi finds herself hunted by a far more unpredictable force. For the first time, her greatest adversary is not the supernatural, but the living.

movies.title: Never After Dark
movies.cast: Moeka Hoshi, Kurumi Inagaki, Kento Kaku
movies.description:
Presented in Japanese with English subtitles
A wandering medium, Airi spends her life guiding restless spirits out of the world of the living. As she digs deeper into the house’s past, a secret comes to light – and Airi finds herself hunted by a far more unpredictable force. For the first time, her greatest adversary is not the supernatural, but the living.

movies.title: News From Home
movies.description: Akerman was 26 years old and living in New York City, away from her native Belgium and her mother, when she teamed with DP Babette Mangolte to film this diary/essay/poem in subway stations and on street corners, their images to eventually be paired with…

movies.title: News from Home + Interior NY Subway, 14th Street
movies.description: Introduction by series curator Genevieve Yue on Sunday, November 1st

movies.title: NicoláS GuilléN LandriáN Shorts Program
movies.director: Nicolás Guillén Landrián This program of five short films offers an introduction to the subversive Cuban experimental filmmaker and painter Nicolás Guillén Landrián. En un bario Viejo
movies.description: This program of five short films offers an introduction to the subversive Cuban experimental filmmaker and painter Nicolás Guillén Landrián. En un bario Viejo (1963) 9min, digital Life in one of Havana's old neighborhoods is captured on film Los del baile (1965) 6min, digital People dance to a performance by Pello el Afrokán’s Orchestra in this short video essay. Like P.M. , the government censored Los del baile for presenting an “undesirable” image of Havana nightlife. Ociel del Toa (1965) 17min, digital A poetic rendering of the lives of the people who inhabit the banks of the Toa River in Cuba’s Oriente province. Reportaje (1966) 19min, SD file A group of the Cuban poor convene to discuss politics and eventually set a large rag-doll ablaze in an act of collective exorcism. Coffea Arábiga (1968) 18min, digital Commissioned by the government to produce a propaganda film on Cuban coffee, Landrián smuggled dissent into the project, turning it into a cinematic Trojan horse which drew a ban after the so-called Cuban “coffee plan” fell apart. Taller de Linea y 18 (1971) 15min, SD file Landrián’s first project to feature conventional documentary-style narration offers audiences a glimpse inside the workings of a bustling Havana factory.

movies.title: Night on Earth
movies.description: Jarmusch’s career-long fascination with at-home-in-the-world wanderers finds its perfect expression in this anthology piece with a Tom Waits soundtrack and Independent Spirit Award-winning cinematography by Elmes, set simultaneously in five different…

movies.title: Nighthawks
movies.description: Sergeant DaSilva (Stallone) has to track down and neutralize two terrorist threats in this tense neo-noir. Malmuth’s solo directorial debut, the project was plagued by production problems, with Stallone himself stepping in to help direct and re-edit aspects of the dark cat-and-mouse game. Despite being used as a shooting location for the 57th and 42nd Street stations within the film, a pesky Hoyt-Schermerhorn sign made its way into the film’s final cut.

movies.title: Nitrate Kisses
movies.description: Barbara Hammer’s pioneering first feature weaves together a liberating portrait of queer sexuality through a dizzying mix of archival and original footage: interviews, sexual imagery, and excerpts of documentary and narrative films from the 1930s, including the first gay film from the U.S., James Sibley Watson and Melville Webber’s Lot in Sodom (1933). Hammer’s editing juxtaposes contrasting images and sounds and brings past and present into an intimate and unexpected dialogue. With sections that explore, among other matters, the sexuality of American author Willa Cather and the status of lesbians in the Third Reich, Hammer’s film boldly pulls back the curtain on the queer experience. A Strand Releasing release. Restored by BB Optics (Mackenzie Lukenbill, Restoration Technician). Supported by Frameline and The Estate of Barbara Hammer. Restoration overseen by Brydie O’Connor.

movies.title: No Other Choice
movies.description: South Korea’s Academy Awards submission for Best Foreign Film is being hailed by critics as an utter masterpiece and earned a rapturous nine-minute standing ovation at this year’s Venice Film Festival. No Other Choice follows one man’s berserk search for a new job after he is abruptly laid off from the paper company where he worked for 25 years. The visionary Park Chan-wook ( Oldboy , Decision to Leave ) helms this captivating black-comedy thriller—one of the most highly anticipated and acclaimed films of the season—adapted from Donald E. Westlake’s 1997 novel The Ax .

movies.title: NOFX: 40 Years of Fuckin' Up
movies.description: 40 YEARS OF FUCKIN' UP is SPINAL TAP, but real. It's a film about the infamous, fairly unfamous, and beloved punk rock band NOFX. This is the unbelievable story about how a group of untalented, drug-addicted teenage punks somehow became the most successful independent band in history – and they did it haphazardly, entirely on their own.

movies.title: Nosferatu (1922)
movies.description: In the town of Wisbourg, estate agent Mr. Knock is pleased to receive a commission from Count Orlok to find a house for him. He dispatches his young assistant, Hutter, to Orlok's castle in the far-off Carpathians. He tells Hutter to get him to buy the vacant house just opposite Hutter's own. Hutter arrives at his destination safely and the Count is all too eager to buy the proposed property, especially after he sees a photo of Hutter's pretty young wife Ellen. Hutter soon realizes the evil he's dealing with and is locked away while Orlock makes his way by ship to Wisbourg. As Orlok travels to Wisbourg, plague descends in his wake and the people of Wisbourg begin to sense the coming of evil. Hutter eventually escapes Orlok's castle, determined to return home as quickly as possible, but exhausted and ill, finds himself in hospital. Hutter nonetheless arrives home the same day as Orlok and the townsfolk begin to panic over the increasing number of deaths.

movies.title: Nostalghia
movies.description: Andrei Tarkovsky explained that in Russian the word nostalghia conveys “the love for your homeland and the melancholy that arises from being far away.” This debilitating form of homesickness is embodied in his film about Russian intellectual Andrei Gorchakov doing research in Italy, who becomes obsessed with the Botticelli-like beauty of his translator Eugenia, as well as with the apocalyptic ramblings of a self-destructive wanderer named Domenico. Written with frequent Michelangelo Antonioni collaborator Tonino Guerra ( L’Avventura ), this mystical and mysterious collision of East and West incorporates an unnamed German Shepherd in a small role—a quiet nod to Tarkovsky's own pup and broader love of dogs.
