movies.title: Nous (We)
movies.description: A Malian mechanic; the filmmaker’s sister, a healthcare worker; the acclaimed author Pierre Bergounioux; banlieue teenagers playing Uno… What ties the disparate subjects of Diop’s film together is, in one sense, geographical happenstance—they all…

movies.title: Nuestra Escena: Punk Across Latin America
movies.description: In response to colonization, dictatorships, class inequality, and a myriad of contemporary societal maladies, young people throughout the Latin American region have built rebellious scenes that allow for radical creative expression, community, and revolutionary ideology—alongside classic teenage debauchery. Influenced by pioneering Latin proto-punk bands such as Los Saicos and Joelho de Porco, and internationally known rock bands like the Sex Pistols and The Dead Kennedys, vibrant punk scenes began popping up in the 1970s in countries like Peru, Mexico, Colombia, Argentina, and Brazil, and even spread to the Latin diaspora in American cities like Los Angeles. From lo-res documentaries to works of fiction made on shoestring budgets, this series provides a glimpse into the lives and stories of Latin America’s real punks throughout history.

movies.title: O Brother, Where Art Thou?
movies.description: The Coens’ country-fried, Depression era, quasi-musical take on The Odyssey borrows its title—and more than a bit of its anarchic sense of humor—from Preston Sturges’s Sullivan’s Travels, choreography cues from Busby Berkeley, and rips a few…

movies.title: Oasis
movies.cast: Sol Kyung-gu, \nMoon So-ri
movies.description: In ANIMALS, Los Angeles mayoral candidate Mark Kimball (Ben Affleck) faces those very questions. When he receives an ominous phone call, Mark and his wife Abigail (Kerry Washington) scramble to respond to a threat that could upend their carefully constructed life.

movies.title: Obsession
movies.description: After breaking the mysterious “One Wish Willow” to win his crush’s heart, a hopeless romantic finds himself getting exactly what he asked for. He soon discovers that desire comes at a dark, sinister price in this equally haunting and amusing supernatural horror.

movies.title: Oedipus Rex
movies.description: Seeking source materials from which to forge a new “primal cinema,” Pasolini delved into the storehouse of mythic heritage. Taking on Sophocles’s Oedipus Rex, he begins with a prologue set in prewar Italy, and goes on to defy expectation throughout,…

movies.title: Of Father And Sons: The Bakri Family On Screen
movies.description: Palestinian actor, filmmaker, and activist Mohammad Bakri worked onstage and on screen from the early 80s until his passing in December 2025. A highly regarded figure, Bakri is considered a founding father of Palestinian cinema. That designation also applies literally, since Bakri’s six children—notably Saleh, Ziad, Adam, and Mahmood—are themselves respected actors and occasional filmmakers. Known as some of the best in the region, the Bakris have appeared in many beloved films and television shows produced across the globe, often performing alongside each other. With two high-profile films featuring various members of the family coming out this year, and in memory of their patriarch, there has never been a more appropriate time to explore some of the incredible work of this talented film family.

movies.title: Off The Pig + Black Panthers
movies.description: Shown in celebration of the 60th anniversary of the Black Panther Party’s founding, these two shorts—one by acclaimed French New Wave auteur Agnés Varda and the other from the Newsreel collective—offer an opportunity to hear directly from Huey P. Newton, Eldridge Cleaver, and other Black Panthers during a pivotal moment for the organization. Followed by a panel discussion Off the Pig (Newsreel #19) (1968) Dir. San Francisco Newsreel With Eldridge Cleaver, Huey P. Newton, Bobby Seale 14min Comprised of interviews with Black Panther Party Minister of Defense Huey P. Newton and Minister of Information Eldridge Cleaver, footage of demonstrations, and drawings from Emory Douglas, this documentary from the nonprofit San Francisco Newsreel serves as a compelling portrait of the party’s leadership in 1967. Black Panthers (1968) Dir. Agnès Varda With Huey P. Newton, Eldridge Cleaver, Bobby Seale, Kwame Ture 28min, DCP In the summer of 1968, master of the French New Wave Agnés Varda turned her camera to Oakland, California to document meetings organized by the Black Panther Party in an effort to free founder Huey P. Newton.

movies.title: Okja
movies.description: The titular beast is a gentle, lumbering, lovable “super pig” created by big agribusiness, peacefully raised in the South Korean countryside by young Mija (Ahn Seo-hyun) before being spirited off to the US, sweeping both pet and owner into a conflict…

movies.title: Oldboy
movies.description: Homer with a ball-peen hammer. Kidnapped and stuffed in a hole without explanation for 15 years of solitary confinement, when Oh Dae-su (Choi Min-sik) is suddenly let loose on the streets, he’s stone-cold pissed off and very, very dangerous. Winner of…

movies.title: Omar
movies.description: Arrested after the killing of an Israeli soldier and tricked into an admission of guilt by association, a young Palestinian baker who routinely climbs over the separation wall running through Jerusalem to meet up with his girlfriend agrees to work as an informant. Nominated for the Best Foreign Feature Academy Award in 2014, Hany Abu-Assad’s film is both a thriller and a romance set against the tension of the Israeli occupation. Presented with the support of Friendly Strangers Studios. @friendlystrangersstudios on instagram.

movies.title: On Golden Pond
movies.description: Art can hold a mirror to reality, and provide a venue to catharsis in its retelling. The 1981 family drama On Golden Pond chronicles the relationship between curmudgeon Norman (Henry Fonda, in his final film appearance) and his estranged daughter Chelsea (Jane Fonda). When Norman and his wife Ethel (Hepburn) agree to care for Billy—the son of Chelsea’s new boyfriend—at their summer home, a blossoming new relationship provides an opportunity to heal old wounds. The latter Fonda had purchased the rights to the play on which the film was based specifically in hopes her father would portray the patriarch, and to provide an opportunity to recount a father-daughter rift that paralleled their real-life relationship.

movies.title: On The Silver Globe
movies.description: After abandoning a dystopian future Earth, a small band of dissident astronauts crash-land on an earthlike planet and set out to establish a new human civilization—only to discover in time that they carry the seeds of their own slow demise and a new mythology. Polish writer-director Andrzej Żuławski adapted On the Silver Globe from The Lunar Trilogy , novels written between 1901 and 1911 by his grand-uncle, Jerzy Żuławski. After a year of filming in 1976 and 1977, Polish authorities shut down the production and ordered all materials destroyed, but the studio, cast, and crew preserved reels, costumes, and props, allowing Żuławski to devise a conclusion in time to screen the film at Cannes in 1988. RogerEbert.com proclaimed, “Even out of time, even incomplete, even now that its director is gone for good, On the Silver Globe endures and its beautiful power will never dim.”

movies.title: Once Upon a Time in China
movies.description: No one wields a ’Scope frame with quite the same flexibility and dynamism as Hark, and the spectacular, Sergio Leone–inspired Once Upon a Time in China—perhaps the crucial film of the 1990s wuxia revival—shows Hark at his most flamboyant, keeping…

movies.title: Once Upon a Time in China II
movies.description: No one wields a ’Scope frame with quite the same flexibility and dynamism as Hark, and the spectacular, Sergio Leone–inspired Once Upon a Time in China II shows Hark at his most inspired, keeping up with the human whirlwind that is Jet Li, here…

movies.title: Once Upon a Time in China III
movies.description: In Jet Li’s third outing as the legendary Wong Fei-hung, master of both inflicting pain and relieving it, Wong and Rosamund Kwan’s “13th Aunt” travel from Foshan to Beijing to meet with his father, there finding preparations underway for a…

movies.title: One Battle After Another
movies.description: Washed-up revolutionary Bob (DiCaprio) exists in a state of stoned paranoia, surviving off the grid with his spirited, self-reliant daughter, Willa (Infiniti). But when his evil nemesis (Penn) resurfaces after 16 years and Willa goes missing, the aging radical finds himself thrust back into the action in order to find her, causing both father and daughter to pay the price for Bob’s past life. Loosely riffing on the narrative arc of Vineland , but updated to the modern world of ICE raids and new American brownshirts, Paul Thomas Anderson’s ( There Will Be Blood , Boogie Nights ) Best Picture winner includes perhaps the most Pynchonian concept not penned by the master himself: a cadre of American fascists that call themselves “The Christmas Adventurers Club.”

movies.title: Onibaba
movies.description: During a sweltering summer in 14th century Japan, a mother and her daughter-in-law survive by murdering lost samurai and selling their armor for food. That is, until a suitor comes between them. As their relationship unravels in a blaze of lust and distrust, the film’s stark black-and-white cinematography, tense, percussive score, and supernatural liberties push Onibaba into an impressionistic mode of storytelling, one that is erotic, disturbing, and surreal. Bodies thrash through sinister waist-high grass, corpses pile up and begin to rot, and still the air grows thick with desire. Part folk-horror, part social critique, part cinematic rendering of Noh theater, Kaneto Shindō’s pivotal piece of ‘60s Japanese cinema is a feral phantasmagoria that defies easy categorization.

movies.title: Ornette: Made In America
movies.description: Returning in 1983 to his home in Fort Worth, Texas, documentary footage and dramatic scenes recall legendary performer and composer Ornette Coleman's rise from oppressed youth to cultural pioneer. Featuring some of the first music-video-style footage of its time, director Shirley Clarke and producer Kathelin Hoffman employed innovative techniques to capture the extraordinary vision of the man behind the music. Pynchon, a known jazz aficionado, based V. ’s alto sax player McClintic Sphere on Coleman.

movies.title: Other Mommy
movies.cast: Jessica Chastain, Jay Duplass, Arabella Olivia Clark, Dichen Lachman, Arian Moayed, Karen Allen
movies.description: Jessica Chastain plays both sides of motherhood in this unsettling supernatural thriller, as a loving mom and the terrifying presence that begins haunting her daughter’s home. Jay Duplass and Dichen Lachman co-star in a nightmare where the simple words “there’s someone in the house” take on a whole new meaning. And if a ball pit doesn’t already make you nervous, this movie may have some ideas for you. See it with friends, or bring your mom and have plenty to talk about on the way home.

movies.title: Out Of The Closet And Into The Co-Op: Early Queer Cinema At The Film-Makers’ Cooperative
movies.description: Programmed by Matt McKinzie and Conor Williams The Film-Makers' Cooperative (a.k.a. The New American Cinema Group), founded in 1961 by a group of artists including Jonas Mekas, Jack Smith, and Ken and Flo Jacobs, is an essential New York organization for experimental film. In 1964, Mekas and the Jacobses were arrested for screening Smith’s queer classic Flaming Creatures at the New Bowery Theater. The ensuing court case catalyzed a national conversation surrounding censorship and freedom of artistic expression, and solidified the Cooperative’s reputation as a countercultural nexus for filmmakers on the margins. As the Cooperative enters its 65th year in operation, this program seeks to highlight the exceptional way in which the organization served as an incubator for early queer cinema in the wake of that groundbreaking trial. Queer and trans Americans are currently under threat from the federal government in ways not seen since the time of the Cooperative’s founding. In the 1960s, when most of these films were made, LGBTQ+ people faced intense repression and police violence. These short films, born out of that atmosphere of oppression, found new ways of formal expression that encouraged queer artists to be out and free. Un chant d’amour (1950) Dir. Jean Genet 25min; 16mm The only film by the famed French writer Jean Genet, Un chant d’amour ’s depiction of the erotic fantasy of a gay male prisoner and that of his captor influenced everyone from Robert Bresson to Kenneth Anger. A print of Genet’s film arrived in the United States in 1964 for distribution at The Film-Makers’ Cooperative. Earlier that year, Coop co-founders Jonas Mekas and Ken and Flo Jacobs were arrested for screening another queer classic, Jack Smith’s Flaming Creatures . In order to raise money for a legal defense fund, Mekas hosted a benefit screening of Genet’s film—and was once again arrested. Amphetamine (1966) Dir. Warren Sonbert 10min; Digital The transgressive debut film of Warren Sonbert depicts a group of preppy, young gay men lounging, kissing, and taking intravenous drugs in an enclosed space, underscored by the lush music of the Supremes. A groundbreaking pre-Stonewall document of queer intimacy, euphoria, and community-building that pays visual homage to none other than Alfred Hitchcock’s Vertigo . Song for Rent (1969) Dir. Jack Smith 7min; Digital In this subversive and tongue-in-cheek short, Jack Smith appears in drag as cadaverous matron Rose Courtyard (inspired by Rose Kennedy). Dressed completely in red, the wheelchair-bound Rose sits ceremoniously under an American flag, the floor littered with corpses, while Kate Smith sings “God Bless America” on the soundtrack. Private Imaginings and Narrative Facts (1966) Dir. Edward Owens 6min; Digital Edward Owens, a Black gay filmmaker and integral yet long-overlooked figure in the early history of the Film-Makers’ Cooperative, sumptuously crafts (in the words of his mentor Gregory Markopolous) a “sensitive, poetic evocation” consisting of “a montage of still and moving images, mixing and alternating Black people and white people, fantasy and reality, a presidential suite and a mother's kitchen.” Jerovi (1966) Dir. José Rodriguez-Soltero 6min; 16mm A sexual probe of the Narcissus myth, this astonishing early short by gay Puerto Rican filmmaker José Rodriguez-Soltero depicts a young man—clothed at first in rich brocade, and later nude—practicing self-love in a garden. Like Edward Owens, Rodriguez-Soltero was a key figure in the early history of the Film-Makers’ Cooperative whose oeuvre was nearly lost to time. Behind Every Good Man… (1966–67) Dir. Nikolai Ursin 7min; 16mm This groundbreaking short, recently inducted into the National Film Registry by the Library of Congress, follows a day in the life of a Black trans woman. As noted by Maya Simone Cade of the Black Film Archive, Ursin’s film is a “hopeful documentary [and] vital cultural document” wherein the subject is allowed to “narrate her own life, desires, and ambitions.” All Women Are Equal (1972) Dir. Marguerite Paris 15min; Digital Recently digitized in 2K by The Film-Makers’ Cooperative in collaboration with Cinebox and the London Short Film Festival, All Women Are Equal offers a portrait of Paula, a trans woman living in Nottingham, England in the early 1970s. Produced, directed, shot, and edited by veteran lesbian filmmaker Marguerite Paris, the film is historically significant for its sensitive and non-expolitative treatment of its subject. Dyketactics (1974) Dir. Barbara Hammer 4min; Digital Created at the height of both the second-wave feminist movement and Seventies gay liberation, Barbara Hammer’s Dyketactics is a landmark filmic evocation of sapphic intimacy and desire. Described by the filmmaker as “a popular lesbian ‘commercial,’” the film depicts “110 images of sensual touching montages in A, B, C, D rolls of ‘kinaesthetic’ editing.”

movies.title: Pale Flower
movies.description: “Yakuza gangster Muraki (Ryo Ikebe) is released from prison after serving time for murder. At the gambling parlor, he meets the young and mysterious Saeko (Mariko Kaga), drawn towards danger and excitement. Together, they drift into an inexorable descent of self-destruction. A depiction of the underworld of yakuza with stark black-and-white imagery, among its highlights are the gambling sequences where the clattering of cards melts into Toru Takemitsu and Yūji Takahashi’s score. The two leads give stellar performances as Ikebe’s world-weary presence and forlorn posture match with Mariko Kaga’s enigmatic aura and piercing gaze. Widely regarded as one of the greatest Japanese films, Shinoda’s noir film cemented him as a leading voice of the Japanese New Wave.” - Akinaru Rokkaku

movies.title: Palestine ‘36
movies.description: In 1936, Yusuf (Karim Daoud Anaya) oscillates between his rural home in Mandatory Palestine and an increasingly restless Jerusalem. Chronicling what would become the largest uprising against Britain’s 30-year colonial project in the region, writer-director Annemarie Jacir (who was last at BAM for a full retrospective in 2018) returns with her most ambitious project to date. Anchored by performances from Hiam Abbass ( Succession ) and Saleh Bakri ( All That’s Left of You ), the only feature to shoot in Palestine in the last two years arrives at a critical time. Advance screening followed by a Q&A with Annemarie Jacir on Mar 20, followed by our run of the film starting Mar 27

movies.title: Pan Labyrinth 20th Anniversary
movies.description:
Celebrating its 20th Anniversary, Guillermo del Toro’s PAN'S LABYRINTH is an Academy Award–winning dark fable set in 1944, five years after the end of the Spanish Civil War. Eleven-year-old Ofelia (Ivana Baquero, in a mature and tender performance) comes face to face with the horrors of fascism when she and her pregnant mother are uprooted to the countryside, where her new step-father (Sergi López), a sadistic captain in General Francisco Franco’s army, hunts down Republican guerrillas refusing to give up the fight. The violent reality in which Ofelia lives merges seamlessly with her fantastical interior world when she meets a faun in a decaying labyrinth and is set on a strange, mythic journey that is at once terrifying and beautiful. In his revisiting of this bloody period in Spanish history, del Toro creates a vivid depiction of the monstrosities of war infiltrating a child’s imagination and threatening the innocence of youth.
Written and directed by del Toro, and produced by his company, Tequila Gang, Guillermo del Toro'sPAN'S LABYRINTH was nominated in six categories at the 79th Academy Awards® and took home three Oscar® wins: Best Achievement in Cinematography, Best Achievement in Art Direction, and Best Achievement in Makeup. Across all awards, the film has received 106 wins from 115 nominations.

movies.title: Pank: Origins Of Punk In Chile
movies.description: In response to Augusto Pinochet's dictatorship and the wider political landscape of Chile in the 1980s, young people throughout the nation began to explore music as a form of expression and resistance. Replete with interviews from members of Fiskales ad-hok, Dadá, Pinochet Boys, Políticos Muertos, and Núñez’s personal experience, PANK showcases the importance of chronicling a recent history that almost slipped through the cracks

movies.title: Paprika
movies.description: The fourth and final film by Kon takes place in a not-too-distant future in which therapists, using a new technology called DC Mini, are able to record the dreams of psychiatric patients. All well and good, until a raid on the lab leads to the loss of the…

movies.title: Paris Belongs To Us
movies.description: Before the official onset of the French New Wave with Truffaut’s The 400 Blows and Godard’s Breathless , critic-turned-filmmaker Jacques Rivette had already started working on his debut feature. The tale of a young literature student (Schneider) and her group of young friends bonded over the death of an acquaintance serves as a time capsule of the social and aesthetic milieu of post-World War II Paris, mirroring a lot of the paranoia and looming spectre of nuclear annihilation permeating through so much of Pynchon’s work.

movies.title: Paris Was a Woman
movies.description: Q&A with filmmakers Greta Schiller & Andrew Weiss from October 16th-October 18th

movies.title: Peking Opera Blues
movies.description: Set in the newly established, vulnerable Republican China of 1913, Peking Opera Blues is a fizzily exuberant, chaotically colorful espionage thriller/screwball romance/slapstick social satire/costume drama pageant that bends genres and genders at will,…

movies.title: Peppermint Frappé
movies.description: Chaplin and Saura’s electric creative partnership began with this perverse play on Alfred Hitchcock’s (already quite perverse!) Vertigo, in which meek doctor José Luis López Vázquez becomes besotted with his childhood friend’s bride (Chaplin),…

movies.title: Petro
movies.description: From campaign announcement in September 2021 through to election day, Sean Mattison had unprecedented access to the campaign of now president of Colombia Gustavo Petro. This portrait of the nation’s most charismatic (and polarizing) politician traces historic upheaval in Colombia, and the highs and lows of a progressive movement that altered its political landscape.

movies.title: Pillion
movies.description: Timid Colin (Melling) is swept off his feet when Ray (Skarsgård), an enigmatic, impossibly handsome biker, takes him on as his submissive. Subversive, sexy, and surprisingly tender, this unconventional romance between an inquisitive young gay man and his leatherman lover was written by director Harry Lighton, based on the 2020 novel Box Hill by Adam Mars-Jones.

movies.title: Pink Floyd – The Wall
movies.description: Featuring sparse dialogue and a mesmerizing combination of experimental animation and live action, Alan Parker’s visualization of a landmark album lives in a limbo between music video and narrative film. Tracing the trials and tribulations of rock star Pink, driven to madness by the privilege of stardom and trauma of his upbringing, the kaleidoscopic odyssey is at times horrifying and others jubilant. Pink Floyd — The Wall is the visualized embodiment of the angst reverberating through the rock opera concept album of the same name, which established Pink Floyd as perhaps the distinctive voice in prog rock. Preceded by a special video introduction by Lim Giong

movies.description: Introduction by series curator Anri Vartan on Sunday, October 18th

movies.title: Possible Love
movies.cast: Jeon Do-yeon, Sul Kyung-gu, Zo In-sung
movies.description: In such searing dramas as Secret Sunshine (NYFF45) and Burning (NYFF56), the great filmmaker Lee Chang-dong pierces the heart of contemporary South Korea, laying bare the scars of personal trauma and socioeconomic grievance. His extraordinary latest concerns two middle-aged couples from different walks of life who become unlikely acquaintances. Working-class Mi-ok (Jeon Do-yeon) and Ho-seok (Sul Kyung-gu), who have been together since middle school and are the parents of a taciturn 10-year-old, are still reckoning with the fallout from Ho-seok’s firing from his factory job after a violently suppressed labor union strike. The well-off Ye-ji (Cho Yeo-jeong) and Sang-woo (Zo In-sung) are a documentary filmmaker and her businessman husband; Ye-ji has decided to make a movie about job layoffs and wants to make Mi-ok and Ho-seok her main camera subjects. The result is a brilliantly unfolding narrative of simmering resentments, shifting allegiances, sexual tensions, and queries around nonfiction filmmaking ethics that keeps revealing new layers and meanings, anchored by four towering performances that hit a varying array of fragile emotional registers. Possible Love speaks profoundly to our shared current moment of emotional and economic precarity. A Netflix release.

movies.title: Possible Love
movies.cast: Jeon Do-yeon, Sul Kyung-gu, Zo In-sung
movies.description: Four strangers' paths cross by chance, leading to complex emotional entaglements that challenge their existing relationships and force them to confront uncomfortable truths about love and commitment.

movies.title: Powwow People
movies.description: Powwow People is a vérité-style documentary grounded in the rhythms, relationships, and lived experience of a contemporary Native gathering. Rather than entering as outside observers, the filmmakers organized the powwow itself, inviting dancers, singers, vendors, and community members to participate in the making of this film. Structured around the arc of a single day, the film follows four central figures: Gina Bluebird, who frames the powwow’s shape and guides its setup; Ruben Littlehead, the MC whose presence anchors the present moment; Jamie John, a non-binary dancer imagining the future of these traditions; and Freddie Cozad, a singer and drummer considering the past. The film culminates in a 30-minute unbroken shot of a Northern Traditional dance special, drawing the viewer into the textures, movement, and collective presence of the powwow. It is both a reflection of a beloved community and a gesture toward the continuities of Native life. Q&A with Sky Hopinka following the 7pm screenings on 9/11 and 9/12

movies.title: Practical Magic 2
movies.description: Twenty-seven years after Sally and Gillian Owens first bewitched us, Sandra Bullock and Nicole Kidman return with a new generation of family magic and an old curse threatening to unravel it all. The original gave us midnight margaritas, broom mishaps, and Gillian’s eternally enviable wardrobe. Now, the Owens family has another curse to deal with, plus a whole new generation of witches. Bring your whole coven to Alamo Drafthouse and see what kind of trouble the Owens sisters get into this time.

movies.title: Primetime
movies.cast: Robert Pattinson, Merritt Wever, Skyler Gisondo, Phoebe Bridgers, Matthew Maher, Bokeem Woodbine
movies.description: To Catch a Predator host Chris Hansen sets out to make television history

movies.title: Primetime
movies.cast: Robert Pattinson, Merritt Wever, Skyler Gisondo, Phoebe Bridgers, Matthew Maher, Bokeem Woodbine
movies.description: Based on the 2007 Esquire article "Tonight on Dateline This Man Will Die”, Oppenheim’s crime thriller follows To Catch a Predator host Chris Hansen in his mission to make television history. In more than an encomium to a vigilante, the Some Kind of Heaven director exposes the morbid voyeurism that spurred a genre of television and social media in its wake. With a spine-tingling performance from Pattison, oscillating between the surreal and the all too real, Primetime is an immersive drama, thoughtful expose, and a hallucination rolled into one.

movies.title: Primetime
movies.cast: Robert Pattinson, Merritt Wever, Skyler Gisondo, Phoebe Bridgers, Matthew Maher, Bokeem Woodbine
movies.description: In 2006, To Catch a Predator host Chris Hansen sets out to make television history.

movies.title: Prismatic Ground
movies.description: Prismatic Ground is an annual festival in New York City centered on experimental documentary and avant-garde film. Now in its sixth season, the festival presents two exclusive New York premieres at BAM Rose Cinemas, opening night film I Heard That They Are Not Going to See Each Other Anymore by Ka Ki Wong, followed by a new work from acclaimed auteur Nicolas Pereda.

movies.title: Project Hail Mary
movies.description: School-teacher-turned-astronaut Ryland Grace (Gosling) awakes on a space station with no memory of who he is or his mission. As fragments of memory return in bursts, he pieces together his objective to reverse the impact of a space event that hurled Earth into the early stages of an Ice Age, and soon realizes he may not be alone in his quest. Based on the novel by Andy Weir ( The Martian ), Phil Lord and Christopher Miller’s adaptation invokes elements of puppetry and practical effects in its conjuring of Grace’s companion, propelling a visual style reminiscent of some of sci-fi’s trailblazing works.
