movies.title: Stormy Weather
movies.description: Rarely is a single work as richly abundant with the cultural touchstones of its era as Stormy Weather , a proverbial who’s who of the legendary African American actors, singers, musicians, and dancers synonymous with early Hollywood. Boasting an almost exclusively Black cast, Stone’s tale of an aspiring dancer courting a popular singer spotlights not only stars like Lena Horne and Bill Robinson, but also musical talent of the day—like the Nicholas Brothers, Cab Calloway, and Fats Waller. A particularly striking scene features one of the most iconic dance sequences ever put on screen: the acrobatic, precise, and ecstatic routine from the Nicholas Brothers that Fred Astaire deemed the greatest movie musical number he had ever seen.

movies.title: Strangers on a Train
movies.description: “Criss cross.” Hitchcock’s adaptation of Highsmith’s 1951 page-turner kicks off with a casual encounter that reads like a same-sex pickup, as tennis star Guy Haines (Farley Granger) inadvertently agrees to “swap murders” with preening rich kid…

movies.title: Stray Dogs
movies.description: Tsai’s devastating minimalist portrait of urban desolation, destitution and defeat is a gorgeous cinematic lament starring Lee Kang-sheng as a single father of two who ekes out a subsistence living by working as a human signboard while his hungry…

movies.title: Stress Is Three
movies.description: An automobile driving from Madrid to Almeria becomes a veritable pressure cooker in Saura’s formally audacious road movie. The passengers are a well-to-do industrialist, Fernando (Fernando Cebrián); his wife, Teresa (Chaplin, blonde and blasé); and…

movies.title: Summer In Japan
movies.description: Programmed by Jesse Trussell Wind rustling grass in the countryside, a sweltering heat wave ravaging sprawling Tokyo, waves crashing on the shore in Okinawa. Japanese cinema has always had a special affinity for the floating time, exuberant joy, and quiet melancholy of the summer. This series gathers together Japanese summer films spanning seven decades and many of the greatest filmmakers in the nation’s history. From postwar masters (Kurosawa, Ozu) to New Wave iconoclasts (Oshima), ‘80s upstarts (Somai, Obayashi, and Morita), ‘90s icons (Kitano, Iwai, and Aoyama), and contemporary auteurs (Hosoda and Matsumoto), behold the beauty and sadness of the summer.

movies.title: Suspiria
movies.description: Argento’s supernatural horror classic stars Jessica Harper ( Phantom of the Paradise , Pennies from Heaven ) as a young student who discovers a demonic underworld haunting the halls of a dance academy in West Germany. The first film in Argento’s The Three Mothers trilogy, this celluloid nightmare moves between elements of sheer horror and flashes of pure sensory delirium, set to a pounding prog-rock dirge by Goblin. Fifty years on, Suspiria feels as dangerous and decadent as ever.

movies.title: Sweat! 2: The Dampening
movies.description: Programmed by Farihah Zaman Back by popular demand, SWEAT! is a limited series that celebrates the stinking, visceral, undeniably human sight of perspiration on-screen. Films that sweat dive below the surface, deep into our pores, to betray characters’ most unspeakable desires. Whether motivated by bloodlust or liberation, the taboo or transcendent, the audacity to defy the gods or the power to touch the divine, sweat illuminates both the tragic cost and exquisite ecstasy of being alive. Where Hollywood insists on presenting the powdered face of perfection, these films revel in the moments that leave us wrung out and dripping wet.

movies.title: Sweet Sweetback’S Baadasssss Song
movies.description: After saving a Black Panther from racist cops, a Black male prostitute goes on the run from “the man” with the help of the ghetto community and some disillusioned Hells Angels. Deemed by Huey P. Newton “the first truly revolutionary Black film made,” Peebles' landmark 1971 film catalyzed a whole genre of blaxploitation, a cultural touchstone of the ‘70s. Soundtracked by the thumping basslines of then-unknown Earth, Wind & Fire, Peebles’ opus became the blueprint for not just the genre it birthed, but soul music’s ongoing symbiosis with cinema.

movies.title: Sympathy for Mr. Vengeance
movies.description: Introduction by LEENALCHI and a post-screening Q&A with composer Jang Young Gyu moderated by Goran Topalovic, October 3rd

movies.title: Taking Of Pelham 123
movies.description: The third, and most recent, adaptation of John Godey’s 1973 novel, Taking of Pelham 123 charts one of the most iconic subway stories ever put to film. When ‘Ryder’ (Travolta) and his accomplices hijack a 6 train, dispatcher Walter Garber (Washington) is thrust into the position of negotiator. Despite the 6 train setting, most of the film was shot on the track between Hoyt-Schermerhorn and the Transit Museum in Downtown Brooklyn. With a roster of iconic New York/Jersey actors, Scott’s adaptation—arriving near the end of his visually and editorially baroque late period—thrusts a timeless story into the modern era.

movies.title: Talladega Nights: The Ballad Of Ricky Bobby
movies.description: As created by the vocally anti-Bush Adam McKay and Will Ferrell, this satire of the era’s machismo and anti-intellectualism stands as a key text amongst the contemporary satires of the Bush administration and the culture he defined. The hottest name in NASCAR racing, Ricky Bobby ( Ferrell) has it all—a hot wife, a posh life, and best friend Cal Naughton Jr. (John C. Reilly) as his loyal wingman—until flamboyant French Formula One driver Jean Girard (Sacha Baron Cohen) shows up to take it all away. “ Talladega Nights may be brash, unbridled, even unhinged,” the Wall Street Journal proclaimed, “but its cornpone humor is rich in parody, and its craftsmanship is superb.”

movies.title: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles
movies.description: The first film adaptation of Kevin Eastman and Peter Laird’s four anthropomorphic comic book characters, TMNT sends the lovable heroes on a quest to save Splinter. With turtle costumes by Jim Henson’s Creature Shop, the 1990 adaptation employs a combination of puppetry and set design to convey the cartoonish NYC of its ninjutsu-trained brothers. When the Turtles’ reporter pal April exits Manhattan’s City Hall, a keen viewer could note that she actually descends into the Hoyt-Schermerhorn station.

movies.title: Teenage Sex And Death At Camp Miasma
movies.description: Hired to inject fresh blood into the threadbare Camp Miasma slasher-film franchise, ambitious young queer director Kris (Hannah Einbinder, of Hacks ) sets out to cast Billy Presley (Gillian Anderson), the now reclusive actress who played the “final girl” in the film that launched the series. But when the two begin to work together, the connection sparks desire, fear, and delirium. Written and directed by Jane Schoenbrun ( We’re All Going to the World's Fair , I Saw the TV Glow ), Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma opened the Un Certain Regard section at the 2026 Cannes Film Festival, where it won the Queer Palm. According to Time magazine, “Schoenbrun’s delirious third film is their most accomplished, most persuasive and most playful movie yet.” Q&A following the Aug 16, 3pm show with Jane Schoenbrun

movies.title: Testament
movies.description: Sometimes released with the subtitle, “a warzone of memories,” Testament paints a portrait of the Kwame Nkrumah era in Ghanaian history. After two decades of exile following the 1966 coup d’état, government minister-turned-journalist Abena returns to her native country to interview director Werner Herzog, only to instead reckon with her political past through this fragmented, poetic film.

movies.title: Tetsuo: The Iron Man
movies.description: That the world of the future was to be increasingly shaped by Asia was a central tenet of cyberpunk, and so it should come as no surprise that one of the greatest of cyberpunk films came from the Land of the Rising Sun. Man and machine feel the urge to…

movies.title: Tetsuo: The Iron Man
movies.description: A “metal fetishist” driven mad by maggots wriggling in the wounds he has created by driving metal into his flesh runs out into the night and is killed by an automobile. The driver, a businessman, buries the corpse with his girlfriend’s help, but soon begins to discover metal thorns and scabs erupting on his own body. A cult classic written, directed, edited, and produced by Shinya Tsukamoto, Tetsuo: The Iron Man earned a reputation as “one of the most pulverisingly effective sci-fi horror films of the past quarter of a century” ( Sight & Sound ) and comparisons to similarly transgressive works by Sam Raimi, David Cronenberg, and David Lynch.

movies.title: The Addams Family
movies.cast: Raul Julia, Anjelica Huston, Christina Ricci, Christopher Lloyd
movies.description: Among the most perfectly cast Hollywood studio films of the last half-century, cinematographer-cum-director Sonnenfeld’s adaptation of Charles Addams’s macabre recurring New Yorker feature stars Raul Julia as the suave patriarch of the Addams clan…

movies.title: The Adventures Of Buckaroo Banzai Across The 8Th Dimension
movies.description: Buckaroo Banzai (Weller), a cartoonishly over-qualified physicist, neurosurgeon, test pilot, and rock star, must stop alien invaders in this campy sci-fi cult film. Pynchonesque in its overly wacky plot, screenwriter Earl Mac Rauch's genre pastiche is also a reflection of the novelist’s taste for low-brow, pulp, and the sci-fi that colored his youthful media consumption.

movies.title: The Age of Innocence
movies.description: One breathtaking composition follows another in Scorsese’s adaptation of Edith Wharton’s Pulitzer Prize–winning masterpiece about social mores (and taboos) amongst New York’s viperous moneyed classes in late 19th-century New York, brought to life…

movies.title: The American Cinema Under George W. Bush
movies.description: Programmed by Jesse Trussell A defining era in the decline of the American empire, the eight years of the George W. Bush administration are the crucible for our current age. Did American cinema, riding high off the grandeur of 90s blockbusters and the exploding indie film movement, meet the moment? This series looks at a wide range of films—from studio comedies and superheroes, to indie dramas and documentaries—to examine how filmmakers tried to grapple with the aftermath of 9/11, the War on Terror, mass surveillance, atrocities, and the end of the so-called American Century.

movies.title: The Aristocats
movies.description: A big-screen outing for this flight of feline fun from the Disney vaults, the last animated feature to be signed off on by Walt himself is a purr-fect Parisian period piece featuring a family of nose-in-the-air cats who, after being kidnapped away from…

movies.title: The Assassin
movies.description: In China during the Tang dynasty, Nie Yinniang (Shu Qi) works as an assassin, directed to slay corrupt government officials by her master. But a mission failed due to her own mercy begets a more ruthless assignment for the stoic killer: to return to her land of birth and kill the man to whom she was betrothed in youth. Netting a Best Director award at Cannes for Hou Hsiao-Hsien and named the best film of 2015 by Sight & Sound , the film marked the master of the Taiwanese New Wave’s final film before retiring in 2023.

movies.title: The Baffler Presents: Global Texas
movies.description: In conjunction with The Baffler ‘s new issue “Global Texas,” BAM presents a quartet of films interrogating the forbidding terrain and complex history of America’s biggest (and perhaps most American) state. The series kicks off with a rare 35mm presentation of Saba , Texas-born Tommy Lee Jones’ directorial debut The Three Burials of Melquiades Estrada (2006), an unsparing interrogation of border violence and 21st century Manifest Destiny. Martin Ritt’s elegiac masterpiece Hud (1963) starring Paul Newman digs into changing generational attitudes towards agriculture, the ranching industry, and how to conduct business. John Sayles’ indie hit Lone Star (1996) invites viewers to “forget the Alamo” in a sordid tale of corruption and historical amnesia. And the late leftist maverick Robert M. Young’s turn-of-the-century thriller The Ballad of Gregorio Cortez (1982) expands an old folk song (or corrido) about the struggle of a Mexican-American farmer (Edward James Olmos) to clear his name after he’s wrongfully accused of the death of a sheriff's brother.

movies.title: The Ballad Of Gregorio Cortez
movies.description: Adapted from Americo Paredes’ With His Pistol in His Hand , Robert M. Young’s The Ballad of Gregorio Cortez dramatizes the real-life case of Cortez (Edward James Olmos), a Mexican American farmer who became a folk hero after killing an abusive Texas Ranger in self-defense in 1901. With this lyrical yet unsentimental film, Young and his Chicano collaborators put a human face to a widely misunderstood chapter in Texas history. The Ballad of Gregorio Cortez is conversant with the corrido tradition that gives it structure, but also with the stale frontier tropes it challenges, resulting in a work of revisionism and reportage.

movies.title: The Big Lebowski
movies.description: Jeff Lebowski, who actually only answers to “The Dude,” is mistaken for a millionaire of the same name and thrust into an intentionally over-complicated mystery in the Coen Brothers’ sprawling Raymond Chandler-inspired comedy. A predecessor to Pynchon’s Inherent Vice (and Paul Thomas Anderson’s later adaptation), this shaggy dog detective story similarly traces a derelict of the New Left navigating the power systems of Southern California.

movies.title: The Black Cat
movies.description: Loosely based on the 1843 Edgar Allan Poe story of the same name, Fulci’s gory, shuddersome horror follows a small English town plagued by a series of violent acts, all orbiting around one central figure: a cat. An early example of the trademark hyper-violence that would net the Italian master of giallo the title of "The Godfather of Gore,” The Black Cat is macabre and slicked with blood, a vivid exercise in style sure to leave you gasping—and looking sideways at feline friends.

movies.title: The Blair Witch Project
movies.description: The opening text of this era-defining indie horror reads: “In October of 1994 three student filmmakers disappeared in the woods near Burkittsville, Maryland, while shooting a documentary. A year later their footage was found.” In the diegetic filmmakers’ search for the truth of a local myth, the milestone late ‘90s horror calls back to colonial America’s obsession with the supernatural and the idea that something terrifying lingers in the woods at the frontier. Immensely terrifying, simple, and magnetic, the debut from Myrick and Sánchez launched a revival of found footage horror movies throughout the 2000s.

movies.title: The Blob (1988)
movies.description: When ooze-drenched remakes of THE THING and THE FLY brought new life to old horrors in the 1980s, it was only a matter of time before the ante was upped. Cue director Chuck Russell and scripter Frank Darabont, the team behind A NIGHTMARE ON ELM STREET 3: THE DREAM WARRIORS. Also cue the unstoppable human-ingestion machine known as The Blob! Exchanging the quaint science of the original 1950s movie for flesh-ripping mayhem, THE BLOB is a showcase for hallucinogenic goop ‘n’ slime effects, Shawnee Smith (SUMMER SCHOOL) as a tough-as-nails Blob-buster, and a gravity-defying mullet from Kevin “Not Matt” Dillon. This movie demands to be seen in a theater filled with goop-lusting Blobites who demand nothing less than 1000% F-U-N.

movies.title: The Blue Caftan
movies.description: Halim and Mina run a traditional caftan store in one of Morocco’s oldest medinas, and hire Youssef in order to keep up with customer demand. Mina gradually realizes how much her husband is moved by the young man’s presence. Morocco’s official entry for Best International Film at the 95th Academy Awards, The Blue Caftan tells a surprising, tender story of unconditional love and acceptance.

movies.title: The Brides of Dracula
movies.description: Two years after Horror of Dracula, Peter Cushing returned to the role of Doctor Van Helsing, summoned to deal with an outbreak of vampirism at a girls finishing school unleashed by a contaminated aristocrat, Baron Meinster (David Peel). Hammer’s…

movies.title: The Burning Sunset (Aka Killers On Parade)
movies.description: 35mm print imported from Japan (courtesy of the Japan Foundation) A genre-hopping, candy colored comedy-noir-musical, Shinoda’s third feature captures the anarchic spirit of ‘60s filmmaking—recalling Jean-Luc Godard and Seijun Suzuki. When a muckraking journalist is targeted by a gang of youthful assassins (and their pet goat, The End), she must turn to another killer for help. Again working with poet/filmmaker Shuji Terayama as screenwriter, this jazzy satire of Japanese cinema is filled with comic book, pop art energy.

movies.title: The Cassandra Cat
movies.description: In a quiet Czech town, a traveling magician arrives with a beautiful performer and a spectacled cat donning a mysterious pair of sunglasses best left in place. When the shades come off, the feline’s extraordinary vision reveals the hidden nature of everyone it sees, turning the townspeople’s secrets into a riot of color. A key work of the Czechoslovak New Wave, Vojtěch Jasný’s playful fairy-tale allegory combines fantasy, comedy, and sharp social satire, winning both the Special Jury Prize and the C.S.T. Prize at the 1963 Cannes Film Festival.

movies.title: The Cat
movies.description: Three extraterrestrials who have taken the form of earth creatures (two as humans, one a humble cat) team up with a novelist to take down a far more sinister alien. Combining silly animal tropes with pet-swapped action movie mainstays, Lam Ngai Kai (best known for the viciously violent martial arts film Riki-Oh: The Story of Ricky ) renders an epic cross-species battle that is, at times, nonsensical, but always a blast.

movies.title: The Cat Creeps
movies.description: Journalist Terry Nichols enlists a photographer friend to help solve a murder, only to later rely on the help of a much stranger companion: a black cat suspected to be possessed by the spirit of a deceased woman. Toeing the line between true horror and crime melodrama, Erle Kenton ( The Island of Lost Souls ) creeps from mansion to boat brig to dollhouse, weaving around the corners of a plot in which nothing is truly as it appears.

movies.title: The Cat From Outer Space
movies.description: This whimsical romp follows a tabby from, you guessed it, outer space. When a stranded UFO is impounded by the US government, the suits are surprised (and a bit bemused) to find a cat in its pilot seat, donning a special collar that grants the ability to communicate with humans. Jake the cat (played by Rumpler and Amber, brother and sister Abyssinian cats) must seek the help of a scientist to repair his ship and return home in this underrated, quintessential 1970s Disney comedy.

movies.title: The China Syndrome
movies.description: Named for the fictional result of a nuclear meltdown (where reactor fuel melts through the crust of the Earth all the way “to China”), Bridges’ biting thriller traces a reporter’s investigation of a cover-up of safety hazards at a Los Angeles nuclear plant. A gripping and timely depiction of the decade’s nuclear suspicion, the film’s coincidental (and perhaps prescient) release twelve days prior to the Three Mile Island nuclear accident spawned unanticipated conversation and acclaim. Both Fonda and Lemmon received Oscar nods for their portrayals of two strangers bound by a mutually terrifying discovery.

movies.title: The Christophers
movies.description: The estranged children (Corden, Gunning) of a beloved dormant artist (McKellen) hire Lori (Coel), an art restorer and former forger, to pose as a prospective assistant in an effort to access some unfinished canvases they believe to be instrumental to conjuring a worthwhile inheritance. As always, Steven Soderbergh is a master of embedding the formal and technical flourishes of the arthouse inside seemingly populist fare, as exemplified in his Ocean ’s trilogy and last year’s Black Bag (2025). In turns that Deadline deemed an "unusually emotional film for Soderbergh,” McKellen’s and Coel’s tête-à-tête makes for a quintessentially funny and engrossing addition to the director’s oeuvre.

movies.title: The Color of Money
movies.cast: Paul Newman, Tom Cruise, Mary Elizabeth Mastrantonio, Helen Shaver, John Turturro, Bill Cobbs
movies.description: The Hustler isn't what he used to be, but he has the next best thing: a kid who is

movies.title: The Currents
movies.description: Lina (Isabel Aimé González Sola), an accomplished Argentine artist and designer, is in Switzerland to receive an award when she jumps from a bridge into the icy waters below. As she later confesses to a friend, she experienced a moment of deep peace until the thought of her young daughter drew her back to life. But the incident leaves her with a paralyzing fear of water and a growing sense of isolation that threatens both her career and her personal life. Directed by acclaimed filmmaker Milagros Mumenthaler ( Back to Stay ), The Currents is a quietly gripping portrait of a woman on the verge of unraveling.

movies.title: The Curse of Frankenstein
movies.description: Cherished by no less a personage than Martin Scorsese for its “totally uncalled for” graphic violence, The Curse of Frankenstein was a watershed film for both Fisher and Hammer, earning 30 times its budget back in the US alone and establishing the…

movies.title: The Dark Knight
movies.description: Billionaire vigilante Batman (Christian Bale), district attorney Harvey Dent (Aaron Eckhart), and police lieutenant Jim Gordon (Gary Oldman), working together to eliminate Gotham's organized crime, are confronted and confounded by a chaotic criminal mastermind known as the Joker (Heath Ledger). Made in the wake of the 2001 Patriot Act and the rise of technological mass surveillance, Batman’s path to justice in the film recalls the Bush administration’s violation of civil liberties in the name of safety. One of the highest-grossing films of all time, The Dark Knight established the template for the modern super-hero movie, and earned Ledger posthumous Academy, BAFTA, and Golden Globe awards.

movies.title: The Daytrippers
movies.description: Greg Mottola’s feature debut, teeming with deadpan humor and surprising emotional weight, established him as a voice of the ‘90s indie scene. After discovering a love letter written to her husband (Stanley Tucci), Eliza (Hope Davis) rallies her bombastic Long Island family to embark on a quest to uncover the truth. The group—sister (Posey) and pretentious boyfriend (Schriber), her headstrong mom (Anne Meara), and reserved father (McNamara)—traipses New York City in pursuit of answers throughout a detour-filled day that sends the family through the ringer as new revelations come to light and old familial schisms rear their heads.

movies.title: The Deer Hunter
movies.cast: Robert De Niro, John Cazale, John Savage, Meryl Streep
movies.description: In ANIMALS, Los Angeles mayoral candidate Mark Kimball (Ben Affleck) faces those very questions. When he receives an ominous phone call, Mark and his wife Abigail (Kerry Washington) scramble to respond to a threat that could upend their carefully constructed life.

movies.title: The Double
movies.description: Inspired by the Dostoyevsky novella of the same title, Ayoade’s noir-inflected sophomore feature gives a dead game Jesse Eisenberg not one but two juicy parts as both a mousy, long-overlooked office drone, Simon James, and his new colleague, the…

movies.title: The Drama
movies.description: Days before they’re set to tie the knot, a happily engaged couple (Zendaya, Pattinson) is put to the test when one partner discovers some shocking truths about the other. In Kristoffer Borgli’s ( Dream Scenario ) highly-anticipated pairing of two of contemporary cinema’s brightest stars, Zendaya and Pattinson (set to appear onscreen together again this year in Dune: Part Three ) deliver a wedding movie for the ages.

movies.title: The Elephant Man
movies.description: New 4K Restoration Before Blue Velvet cemented Lynch as one of the century’s preeminent directors, he released The Elephant Man , an atmospheric historical drama and important moment in understanding the development of the auteur’s signature style. Set in Victorian England, the black-and-white film follows London surgeon Frederick Treves (Anthony Hopkins) and his developing friendship with freak-show performer John Merrick (John Hurt), challenging perceptions around disability and human dignity. With a stellar supporting cast that includes Anne Bancroft, John Gielgud, and Wendy Hiller, Lynch’s surreal take on a biopic was nominated for eight Academy Awards, cementing his reputation as one of American cinema’s most visionary talents.

movies.title: The Enchanted Desna
movies.description: Introduction by series curator Anri Vartan on Saturday, October 10th

movies.title: The Flavor of Green Tea Over Rice
movies.description: Ozu’s satirical—and ultimately quite touching—portrait of a marriage first seen in a state of quiet unraveling stars Kogure Michiyo and Saburi Shin as a well-off, childless middle-aged couple who find discreet outlets to express their…

movies.title: The Foul King
movies.description: Already a well-established presence in South Korean music, with an ability to work with equal facility in a variety of idioms (experimental, rock, folk, et. al.), Jang got his start in film composing the distinctive score for Kim’s eccentric,…

movies.title: The Girl In The Yellow Jumper
movies.description: As fear spreads across Uganda about a serial killer haunting the highways, an off-duty police officer drives an elderly witness from a remote village back to town. Along the way, he picks up an injured stranger who begins recounting the violent events that led him to the roadside. As the journey unfolds, suspicion grows inside the car, and the officer realizes the truth may be far more dangerous than the story being told.

movies.title: The Good Fairy
movies.description: In 1935, the great German-born American director William Wyler made this film about Luisa Ginglebusher, a sweet-natured yet naive young woman recently released from an orphanage who becomes an usher at a local movie theater. In an attempt to do good, Luisa finds herself wrapped up in a series of hi-jinks and romantic entanglements. The Good Fairy is based on the Hungarian play of the same name by Ferenc Molnár.

movies.title: The Good Fight
movies.description: The fight for the freedom of Loyalist Spain during the 1936-39 civil war pitted an International Brigade of 35,000 civilian soldiers from more than 50 nations against the well-equipped insurgents of Generalissimo Francisco Franco. Aid to Franco came via Italian fighter planes from Mussolini and from the Nazi Condor Legion of Junker bombers sent by Hitler, who wanted to try out his new weaponry in anticipation of the larger war to come. Spurred by their government's failure to aid Spanish democracy, 2,800 American volunteers fought with distinction in the Abraham Lincoln Brigade within the international volunteer army. Lincoln veterans (over 750 were killed in Spain) returned home after the Loyalist defeat to encounter suspicion as "premature anti-fascists." Branded Communist sympathizers, blacklisted for years and unable to get work, many paid dearly for their good fight. Narrated by Studs Terkel, The Good Fight explores a significant gap in our history through its use of newsreels, photographs, interviews with Lincoln veterans and Depression-era music. The eleven surviving veterans of the war who appear in this tough, stirring film share a common pride in their sacrifices of seventy years ago when the rise of world fascism crushed the spirit of democracy in a tragic rehearsal for World War II.

movies.title: The Gorgon
movies.description: In their tireless search for new monsters to add to their menagerie Hammer turned here to Greek mythology, unleashing the fatal gaze of the Gorgon on the residents of a German village, c. 1910. Seven Vandorf residents have in recent years been found…

movies.title: The Gospel According to Ken Russell
The Harder They Come
movies.cast: Jimmy Cliff Music by Jimmy Cliff, Desmond Dekker, The Slickers, The Maytals
movies.description: Perry Henzell’s The Harder They Come marked the epochal cultural moment that first brought reggae to the international stage and made the late Jimmy Cliff a star. Now, 50 years later, the film is as electric as ever. In a Scarface -y blend of crime drama and music, we follow a country boy in search of fame as he journeys through Jamaica as a laborer, recording artist, convict, ganja dealer, and outlaw folk hero.

movies.title: The History of Concrete
movies.description: John Wilson looks to the bedrock of his beloved New York City for inspiration and structure

movies.title: The History of Concrete
movies.description: Following the finale of his TV series, filmmaker John Wilson looks to the bedrock of his beloved New York City for inspiration and structure. Concrete, the world's most widely used building material, appears as an ever-present life force, and John sets out to make the definitive documentary on the matter. To tell this seemingly drab story, he decides to use the industry-approved Hallmark formula to increase his movie's appeal. But his foundation soon begins to crumble – literally and figuratively – as he struggles to balance artistic freedom with the realities of the modern film industry.

movies.title: The History of Concrete
movies.description: A filmmaker applies lessons from a Hallmark movie writing workshop to pitch a documentary about concrete. * Q&A after the Monday, September 21st screenings with director John Wilson * Probably some other ones too just don't know yet

movies.title: The Hound of the Baskervilles
movies.description: An ardent aficionado of the work of Sir Arthur Conan Doyle, Cushing takes over the chambers at 221B Baker Street with aplomb and gives us a Sherlock for the ages in Fisher’s adaptation of the 1902 Holmes adventure of the same name, in which our hero is…

movies.title: The Illiac Passion
movies.description: Markopoulos corralled together the underground’s haute monde—Taylor Mead, Gerard Malanga, Jack Smith, Gregory Battcock and, in the role of Poseidon, Andy Warhol—for his radical reinterpretation of Aeschylus’s Prometheus Bound, in which the…

movies.title: The Immigrant
movies.description: Marion Cotillard has one of her greatest roles as Ewa, a Polish Catholic immigrant newly arrived in Ellis Island, trying to find the means to free her sister from quarantine in a c. 1921 New York City that’s full of lures and snares, among them Joaquin…

movies.title: The Insider
movies.description: Q&A with investigative journalist Lowell Bergman and Pulitzer Prize-winning reporter and podcast host Pablo Torre on Saturday, October 17th

movies.title: The Invite
movies.description: Joe (Seth Rogen) and Angela’s (Olivia Wilde) marriage is on thin ice. When they invite their enigmatic upstairs neighbors (Penélope Cruz and Edward Norton) for a dinner party, the night spirals into unexpected places. Have they reignited the spark or lit the match that burns it all down? A remake of the 2020 Spanish film The People Upstairs , Olivia Wilde’s star-studded take on a dinner party dramedy (written by Will McCormack and Rashida Jones) is a timely portrait of a modern marriage, teeming with wit, belly laughs, and a surprising poignancy.

movies.title: The Island Of Saint Matthews
movies.description: When Kevin Jerome Everson’s inquiry about family photos reveals a lost history, he travels to meet the inhabitants of Westport—a small town just to the west of Columbus, Mississippi—to uncover how his familial record vanished. In this personal investigation of records lost to time and circumstance, Everson convenes with the Wesportians about the great flood of the Tombigbee River in 1973, when some people lost everything. An act of recovery and discovery, Emerson finds a piece of his own history in his pursuit of what was lost.

movies.title: The Lady Eve
movies.cast: Barbara Stanwyck, \nHenry Fonda, \nCharles Coburn
movies.description: In ANIMALS, Los Angeles mayoral candidate Mark Kimball (Ben Affleck) faces those very questions. When he receives an ominous phone call, Mark and his wife Abigail (Kerry Washington) scramble to respond to a threat that could upend their carefully constructed life.

movies.title: The Last Supper
movies.description: In Tomás Gutiérrez Alea’s bold cinematic parable, the owner of a Havana sugar plantation attempts to teach Christianity to his enslaved workers by staging a recreation of the Biblical Last Supper. But when the enslaved refuse to be proselytized and learn that the Count has reneged on his compensatory promises, the film spirals into a darkly ironic critique of colonialism and religion, while showing the resistance of Black peoples.

movies.title: The Legend Of Suram Fortress
movies.description: Codirected by Dodo Abashidze and Sergei Paradjanov, this film is based on a legend from the Caucasus Mountains that tells of the Georgian people’s repeated efforts to construct a fortress amid threats of invasion. The structure continues to collapse until a fortune teller recalls a fateful prophecy. At once simple and marvelous, the story unfolds in a circular manner, while its mythic possibilities are realized in the film’s jewel-like colors and decor.

movies.title: The Little Mermaid
movies.description: This sprightly interpretation of Hans Christian Anderson’s story was eyed by Disney as far back as the days of Snow White and the Seven Dwarves, finally surfacing in 1989. There’s a hot crustacean band, sure, but also a keening grasp of the angst,…

movies.title: The Magician
movies.description: Ingmar Bergman's 1958 feature is an engaging, brilliantly conceived tale of deceit from one of cinema’s premier illusionists. Max von Sydow stars as Dr. Vogler, a nineteenth-century traveling mesmerist and peddler of potions, whose magic is put to the test in Stockholm by the cruel, eminently rational royal medical adviser Dr. Vergérus. The result is a diabolically clever battle of wits that’s both frightening and funny, shot in rich, gorgeously gothic black-and-white.

movies.title: The Man Died
movies.description: During Nigeria’s civil war, writer and activist Wole Soyinka is imprisoned without trial by a military regime determined to silence his dissent. Enduring solitary confinement, torture, and deprivation, he refuses to surrender his commitment to justice, drawing strength from memories of his earlier life as a writer and public intellectual. In secret, he records his experiences on scraps of paper, which are smuggled out of his cell. His words become a beacon of hope and a call to action for others living under oppression, in this work based on the harrowing prison memoir by Nobel laureate Wole Soyinka. Followed by a Q&A with director Awam Ampka

movies.title: The Musical
movies.cast: Will Brill, Gillan Jacobs, Rob Lowe, Nevada Jose, Melanie Herrera, Michael Strassner
movies.description: Doug, a frustrated playwright and middle school theater teacher, learns his ex is dating his nemesis, the school principal. To get revenge and cost him a Blue Ribbon Award, Doug secretly stages the most inappropriate play imaginable.

movies.title: The Night Of The Hunter
movies.description: With an illustrious acting career spanning decades and genres, it’s miraculous that Charles Laughton only stepped behind the camera for one film. Even more miraculous, perhaps, is how the towering English thespian managed to encapsulate so vividly the aesthetic and narrative thrust of the American Southern Gothic in The Night of the Hunter . This eerie story of a serial killer posing as a preacher weaves together elements of Expressionism and the style of silent films, imbuing a haunting tale with a truly singular visual identity. Featuring Robert Mitchum in his finest performance and silent film star Lillian Gish in a late career peak, the film is haunting, tense, and downright sinister. Laughton’s opus would go on to influence a generation of filmmakers including Robert Altman, Spike Lee, and Martin Scorsese.

movies.title: The Ninth Gate
movies.description: Hired by a wealthy collector to authenticate a rarer-than-rare copy of Aristide Torchia’s 17th-century tome The Nine Gates of the Kingdom of Shadows, purported to allow its owner to summon the Devil, New York–based antiquarian book dealer Dean Corso…

movies.title: The North
movies.cast: Bart Harder, Carles Pulido, Olly Bassi
movies.description: The North depicts the grueling and emotional journey of two friends – Chris, a Dutchman (Bart Harder) and Lluis, a Spaniard (Carles Pulido) - who reunite after a decade to re-hike Scotland’s famed 330-mile West Highland Way and Cape Wrath Trail. Brimming with both joy and reservation, they undertake Scotland’s lush, but unpredictable terrain as their days are filled with majestic mountainous vistas, creekside camping, the symphonic strains of wildlife, pummeling rain and a slew of eccentric fellow travelers each on their own paths of self-discovery.

movies.title: The Odyssey
movies.description: Shooting around the globe using 70mm IMAX film cameras, director Christopher Nolan ( Oppenheimer , Tenet , Inception ) transforms Homer’s ancient Greek epic into a luxuriously cast summer blockbuster inspired by Ray Harryhausen’s 1970s sword-and-sandal adventures and informed by Emily Wilson’s admirably savvy 2017 English translation of the original poem. The Odyssey recounts the tale of Ithacan king Odysseus (Matt Damon), confronted by literal monsters and menaces as he returns with his soldiers from the Trojan War, while at home his wife Penelope (Anne Hathaway) and son Telemachus (Tom Holland) send off scheming suitors like Antinous (Robert Pattinson). This film contains sequences of flashing lights which might affect customers who are susceptible to photosensitive epilepsy.

movies.title: The Pawnbroker
movies.description: Lumet investigates the reverberations of the Holocaust two decades later in this haunting depiction of a life altered in its wake. Numb from his experience in a concentration camp, Sol Nazerman (Steiger) lives a life emotionally alienated from those around him in a heartbreaking portrayal of post-Holocaust life. Marking Morgan Freeman’s feature film debut, it’s also Lumet’s first film to shoot at Hoyt-Schermerhorn ahead of 1978’s The Wiz , and one of the major contributors to the deterioration of the Production Code throughout the ‘60s.

movies.title: The Place Without Limits
movies.description: Adapted from José Donoso’s iconic novel by the celebrated Mexican director Arturo Ripstein, The Place Without Limits centers its story on Manuela (Roberto Cobo) and her daughter, who run a fading brothel in the remote setting of El Olivo, Mexico. As the tumbleweed town withers, an unwelcome visitor—once treated as family by the town’s mayor—stirs long‑buried tensions that threaten its fragile peace. Rejected and mislabeled by those around her, Manuela navigates a world ruled by machismo and prejudice. Her resilience and luminous spirit make her the emotional core of a community pushed to the brink. Selected by Mexico as its entry for the Best Foreign Language Film at the 51st Academy Awards, The Place Without Limits is a gripping portrait of dignity and survival in a place determined to extinguish it.

movies.title: The President'S Cake
movies.description: While people across 1990s Iraq struggle to survive the war and food shortages, President Saddam Hussein requires each school in the country to prepare a cake to celebrate his birthday. Despite her efforts to avoid getting picked, 9-year-old Lamia is chosen among her classmates, and must use her wits and imagination to gather the scarcely-available ingredients in this directorial debut that earned the 2025 Caméra d'Or at the Cannes Film Festival

movies.title: The Princess Bride
movies.director: Rob Reiner Based on William Goldman’s novel
movies.cast: Robin Wright, Cary Elwes, Billy Crystal, Mandy Patinkin, Christopher Guest, Wallace Shawn, Carol Kane, Peter Falk

movies.title: The Projectionist + She Was An Acrobat'S Daughter
movies.description: The Projectionist (1970) dir. Harry Hurwitz. With Chuck McCann, Ina Balin, Rodney Dangerfield. 88min; 35mm An imaginative Midtown projectionist (Chuck McCann) whiles away the hours—interrupted by his jerk of a boss, Renaldi (Rodney Dangerfield, in his film debut), and kept company by the movie stars lining the walls of the booth. She Was An Acrobat's Daughter (1937) dir. Friz Freleng 8min; Digital Friz Freleng’s Golden Age animated short parodies the goings-on inside a local movie theater.

movies.title: The Promised Land
movies.cast: Daniel Olbrychski, Wojciech Pszoniak, Andrej Seweryn, Kalin Jedrusik

movies.title: The Samurai And The Prisoner
movies.description: Celebrated Japanese horror director Kiyoshi Kurosawa ( Cure , Serpent’s Path ) explores a new path in this lush treatment of Honobu Yonezawa's prizewinning historical novel, detailing palace intrigue in the court of a samurai nobleman during the Azuchi era at the end of the 16th century. Turning against Oda Nobunaga, the ruthless, power-hungry warlord he previously served, Araki Murashige (Masahiro Motoki, of Departures ) is besieged by Oda’s forces and bedevilled by a series of inexplicable crimes in his household. As tension rises and loyalties fray, Murashige is forced to strategize with Kuroda Kanbei (Masaki Suda, of Kurosawa’s 2024 thriller Cloud ), a samurai envoy sent by Oda and imprisoned by Murashige, while his wife Chiyoho (Yuriko Yoshitaka) and loyalists fight to preserve order.

movies.title: The Scout
movies.description: Director González-Nasser spent six years working as a location scout. In this luminous directorial debut, she brings us into a day in the life of a young scout tasked with finding the perfect interiors for a television pilot. Sofía (Mimi Davila) moves in and out of other people’s intimate spaces and quotidian lives, tweaking her personality just enough to connect while struggling to find balance between her professional and personal worlds. With a mounting stack of parking tickets and the impert

movies.title: The Secret Agent
movies.description: Set in Brazil in 1977, the most awarded film at Cannes this year stars Wagner Moura ( Narcos , Civil War ) as Marcelo, a former teacher and political dissident on the run during the waning years of Brazil’s military dictatorship. Hoping to reunite with his son, he travels to Recife during Carnival but quickly realizes that the city is not the safe haven he expected. Critics are calling Kleber Mendonça Filho’s vivid neo-noir thriller “a masterpiece” ( The Playlist ) and “superb in every way” ( The Guardian ).

movies.title: The Smallest Show On Earth + Box Office Bunny
movies.description: The Smallest Show on Earth (1957) dir. Basil Dearden 80min; DCP The Smallest Show on Earth follows a newly married couple who unexpectedly inherit a dilapidated British cinema and set out to save it from closure, aided—and often undermined—by its eccentric staff. The prolific Basil Dearden, who worked on over 45 films across his career, directs this warmhearted comedy about love, labor, and the quiet heroics of keeping the movies alive. Box Office Bunny (1990) dir. Darrell Van Critters 5min; Digital This delightful Looney Tunes short is set in a massive movie theater situated right above Bugs’ bunny hole and co-stars Elmer Fudd and Daffy Duck.

movies.title: The Social Reckoning
movies.cast: Jeremy Allen White, Betty Gilpin, Mikey Madison, Billy Magnussen, Jeremy Strong, Patrick Fischler, Wunmi Mosaku, Bill Burr
movies.description: Aaron Sorkin returns to the world of THE SOCIAL NETWORK, writing and directing his own sharply scripted dive into the people, power, and paranoia behind Facebook. This time, Sorkin puts whistleblower Frances Haugen (Mikey Madison, ANORA) and Wall Street Journal reporter Jeff Horwitz (Jeremy Allen White, The Bear) at the center of a David-and-Goliath story that threatens to expose the social network’s most guarded secrets. And yes, Jeremy Strong (Succession) is stepping into the Zuckerberg hoodie. Expect rapid-fire dialogue, institutional takedowns, and maybe even some walking and talking. Consider this your latest notification from the algorithm: see this in theaters.

movies.title: The Social Reckoning
movies.cast: Jeremy Allen White, Betty Gilpin, Mikey Madison, Billy Magnussen, Jeremy Strong, Patrick Fischler, Wunmi Mosaku, Bill Burr

movies.title: The Square
movies.description: Nominated for Best Documentary Feature at the 86th Academy Awards, Jehane Moujaim’s film traces the ongoing Egyptian Revolution of 2011, immersing its viewer in the intense emotional drama of young people on the streets of Cairo. The work to claim their rights and create a society of conscience against the toppling of the government serves as an inspiring tribute to the power of citizenry. The May 7 screening will be followed by a Q&A with director Jehane Noujaim and cinematographer Ahmed Hassan, moderated by Alia ElKattan

movies.title: The Stories
movies.description: When aspiring Egyptian pianist Ahmed finds a pen pal in Austrian Liz, their blossoming relationship encourages the former to focus on his ambition of performing a concert during a tumultuous time for the nation. Based on the actual meeting of director Shawky’s parents, this combination of narrative vignettes interspersed with archival footage serves as a decade and nation-spanning time capsule of love in the seventies.

movies.title: The Taking of Pelham One Two Three
movies.description: Introduction by Genevieve Yue and Erika Balsom, with a book signing following the screening, on Saturday, October 3rd

movies.title: The Terminator
movies.description: Too many sequels and an incalculable cultural impact later, it’s sometimes forgotten what a hot and nasty little movie Cameron’s original Terminator was, dropping peak-physique Schwarzenegger into a sleazy Los Angeles of leather bars, punk rockers,…

movies.title: The Testament Of Ann Lee
movies.description: From award-winning writer-director Mona Fastvold ( The World to Come , The Brutalist ) comes the extraordinary true legend of Ann Lee, founder of the Shakers. Academy Award nominee Amanda Seyfried stars as the devotional sect’s irrepressible leader, who preached gender and social equality and was revered by her followers. The Testament of Ann Lee captures the ecstasy and agony of her quest to build a utopia, featuring more than a dozen traditional Shaker hymns reimagined as rapturous movements with choreography by Celia Rowlson-Hall ( Vox Lux ) and original songs and score by Academy Award winner Daniel Blumberg ( The Brutalist ). Join us for a Q&A with director Mona Fastvold, co-writer Brady Corbet, and actor Tim Blake Nelson following the 6:40pm screening on Friday, January 16.

movies.title: The Texas Chain Saw Massacre (1974)
movies.description: Nothing will ever diminish the power of THE TEXAS CHAIN SAW MASSACRE. Shot through a cinéma vérité lens, director Tobe Hooper's ferocious classic follows five friends that fall victim to the grotesque Leatherface and his cannibalistic family. With a beautifully raw DIY aesthetic and powerful performances, this shockingly realistic film revolutionized the horror landscape when it was unleashed on a politically and socially tumultuous America in 1974. Facing controversy and censorship throughout its troubled release, THE TEXAS CHAIN SAW MASSACRE has stood the test of time to become a landmark film and cultural milestone.

movies.title: The Thin Man
movies.description: Nick, a former detective, retired when he married the wealthy heiress Nora, instead content to spend his days galavanting around high society. Abetted by his wife’s restless desire for adventure, the retired lawman embarks on a whodunnit quest to identify a missing inventor. Despite approaching a century since its release, The Thin Man flows with a miraculously contemporary pace and humor, replete with quick-firing ratatat from the leading couple, a jaw-dropping overconsumption of alcohol, and some truly belly laugh-inducing reaction shots from canine actor Skippy as Asta.

movies.title: The Three Burials Of Melquiades Estrada
movies.description: After his eponymous best friend (Julio César Cedillo) is killed by a psychotic Border Patrol officer (Barry Pepper), rancher Pete Perkins (Tommy Lee Jones) kidnaps the murderer, forces him to exhume the body, and leads him south of the border so Estrada can receive a hometown burial. In crafting this existential neo-western, Jones and screenwriter Guillermo Arriaga (Amores Perros) were directly inspired by the shooting of Texan teenager Esequiel Hernandez by U.S. Marines in 1997. Jones’ directorial debut is both a taut cowboy thriller and pained, surreal reflection on the American death cult, leavened by startling moments of coal-black humor.

movies.title: The Time That Remains
movies.description: Subtitled “Chronicle of a Present Absentee,” this humorous, heartbreaking film—the final installment in a trilogy that includes Chronicle of a Disappearance and Divine Intervention —is set among the Arab community in Israel and shot largely in homes and places in which director Elia Suleiman’s family once lived. Inspired by his father’s diaries, letters his mother sent to family members who had fled the Israeli occupation, and the director’s own recollections, the film spans from 1948 until the present, recounting the saga of Suleiman’s family in elegantly stylized episodes. Inserting himself as a silent observer reminiscent of Buster Keaton, Suleiman trains a keen eye on the absurdities of life in Nazareth.

movies.title: The Travel Companion
movies.description: Simon is a struggling documentary filmmaker enjoying one perk making his practice a little easier: free flights courtesy of his best friend and roommate Bruce, who works for an airline. But when Bruce starts dating Beatrice, Simon starts to worry his infinite supply of pro bono travel may begin to dry up. To top it off, Beatrice is also a filmmaker, and a successful one. In their feature debut, the director duo serves up some delightfully deadpan humor as they unpack the woes of modern filmmaking, jealousy, and the highs and lows of friendship. Q&A with filmmakers on Friday, April 10 moderated by Jesse Trussell, Director, Film Programming at BAM, and on Saturday, April 11 moderated by Dara Messinger, Director of Programming at DCTV.

movies.title: The Treasure of Bitch Islands
movies.description: A phantasmagoric, definition-defying film from perhaps France’s premier underground filmmaker, The Treasure of Bitch Islands begins with the mysterious disappearance of an engineer who has discovered a new energy source, and follows a post-nuclear…

movies.title: The Trouble with Harry
movies.description: The inconvenient corpse, imbued with a sense of tragedy and terror in Hitchcock’s Rope, is the source of borderline-surrealist farce in The Trouble with Harry, his adaptation of Jack Trevor Story’s novel of the same name, a darkly comic tale in which…

movies.title: The Twilight Saga: Breaking Dawn – Part 1
movies.cast: Kristen Stewart, Robert Pattinson, Taylor Lautner

movies.title: The Virgin Suicides
movies.cast:
James Woods, 
Kathleen Turner, 
Kirsten Dunst, 
Josh Hartnett, 
Scott Glenn, 
Michael Paré, 
Danny DeVito
movies.description: In ANIMALS, Los Angeles mayoral candidate Mark Kimball (Ben Affleck) faces those very questions. When he receives an ominous phone call, Mark and his wife Abigail (Kerry Washington) scramble to respond to a threat that could upend their carefully constructed life.

movies.title: The Voice Of Hind Rajab
movies.description: Calling for help from inside a car under heavy Israeli military fire in Gaza, Hind Rajab, a 5-year-old Palestinian girl, reached countless listeners around the world after recordings of her desperate pleas were released online. This new film, made by Academy Award nominee Kaouther Ben Hania ( Four Daughters ) in collaboration with Hind’s family and the Palestine Red Crescent Society, combines archival audio with dramatic recreations of the emergency workers at the call center as they try to dispatch rescuers. Winner of the Grand Jury Prize at the 2025 Venice Film Festival, this powerful film compels us to face this tragedy with open eyes.

movies.title: The Voice Of Hind Rajab
movies.description: Calling for help from inside a car under heavy Israeli military fire in Gaza, Hind Rajab, a 5-year-old Palestinian girl, reached countless listeners around the world after recordings of her desperate pleas were released online. This new film, made by Academy Award nominee Kaouther Ben Hania ( Four Daughters ) in collaboration with Hind’s family and the Palestine Red Crescent Society, combines archival audio with dramatic recreations of the emergency workers at the call center as they try to dispatch rescuers. Winner of the Grand Jury Prize at the 2025 Venice Film Festival, this powerful film compels us to face this tragedy with open eyes. Join us for a Q&A with lead actor Saja Kilani following the 7:30pm screening on Tuesday, January 13.

movies.title: The Wailing
movies.description: Introduction by composer Jang Young Gyu on Saturday, October 3rd

movies.title: The Warriors
movies.description: “Waaarriors! Come out and play-ay!” Falsely accused of responsibility for the assassination of New York’s most powerful ganglord during a citywide summit in the Bronx’s Van Cortlandt Park, Swan (Michael Beck) and his fellow Warriors now have to…

movies.title: The Warriors
movies.description: Accused of a murder they didn't commit, the members of The Warriors eponymous gang end up with targets on their back. In the Walter Hill-directed flick (with a screenplay by Hill and David Shaber), the Warriors traverse the city in a mission to evade death and prove their innocence. In a particularly memorable moment, the gang pulls into the alleged “96th Street Station” (really Hoyt-Schermerhorn) only to find the cops waiting, forcing them to bolt to the exit. Despite its lukewarm 1979 reception, The Warriors rightfully found its footing as a cult film, beloved for its campy approach to gangland.

movies.title: The Watermelon Woman
movies.description: Cheryl Dunye made cinematic history with The Watermelon Woman , the first American feature to be directed by a Black lesbian as well as an incisive, humorous critique of classic Hollywood's racist stereotypes. Dunye plays a video store employee and burgeoning filmmaker who sets out to make a documentary on the Watermelon Woman (Lisa Marie Bronson), an actress who specialized in "mammy" roles for Hollywood productions of the 30s and 40s. As Cheryl uncovers the Watermelon Woman's identity she not only learns about a secret behind-the-scenes interracial romance but also begins one of her own with Diana (Guinevere Turner), a white woman who arouses the ire of Cheryl's best friend Tamara (Valerie Walker).

movies.title: The Wedding
movies.cast: Daniel Olbrychski, Ewa Ziętek,

movies.title: The Wedding Banquet
movies.description: Before scaling Brokeback Mountain, Taiwanese American director Lee made this indie breakout about Wai Tung (Winston Chao, in his film debut), a gay man happily living in Manhattan with his partner who stages a sham marriage between himself and a penniless…

movies.title: The Wiz
movies.description: Michael Jackson and Diana Ross star in The Wizard of Oz offshoot that modernized and added soul to a decades-old story. Reimagining Dorothy’s Technicolor adventure with an entirely Black cast, based on its preceding 1974 staged version, the Sidney Lumet-directed romp is a who’s who of the era’s soul music stars. Quincy Jones oversaw the adaptation of the 1974 musical’s songs by Charlie Smalls and Luther Vandross, and while it never quite reached the critical highs of the staged version, it shined an ever-spooky light on the Hoyt-Schermerhorn station—where MJ would go on to shoot his “Bad” music video almost a decade later.

movies.title: The Wizard Of Oz
movies.description: The most seen film in cinematic history also features the most iconic dog to ever arf on the silver screen: Terry the Cairn Terrier as the ever-loyal Toto. While the prismatic story of Dorothy’s voyage through a magical world wasn’t the first Technicolor film put to screen, it surely popularized the technology with its jaw-dropping revelatory transition to vibrant color upon the Kansan’s arrival in Oz. Nominated for five Academy Awards and launching Judy Garland to international stardom, Victor Fleming’s ( Gone with the Wind ) landmark cinematic achievement lives on nearly 90 years after its release as America’s most enduring fairytale story.

movies.title: The Woman Who Poked The Leopard
movies.description: The Woman Who Poked The Leopard (2025) Dir. Patience Nitumwesiga With Stella Nyanzi, Baraka Bah, Kato Bah, Wasswa Bah 108min; DCP Uganda, South Africa, Germany, US US Premiere An outspoken poet, scholar, and activist, Dr. Stella Nyanzi has become one of the most uncompromising voices of resistance in Uganda. After publicly criticizing President Yoweri Museveni online, she was arrested in 2018 and imprisoned, where severe mistreatment led to the loss of her pregnancy. Undeterred, she returned to the public arena in 2020 to campaign for parliament, challenging Museveni’s continued rule. A radical feminist and advocate for queer rights in a country where homosexuality is criminalized, Nyanzi faces constant harassment from authorities determined to silence dissent. Interweaving footage from the campaign trail with archival scenes of protest and repression, alongside intimate moments with her three teenage children, the story reveals both Uganda’s fraught political landscape and the personal toll borne by those who dare to resist. Screening with a video introduction from director Patience Nitumwesiga Preceded by: A Kalabanda Ate My Homework (2017) Dir. Raymond Malinga 7min; DCP Uganda Tendo, a pupil, shows up to class one day without homework - claiming that a "Kalabanda" ate it. Who'd believe such a lame excuse? No-one. How will Tendo prove his story? Tendo's mischievous friend Kibe devises a method to protect him from Mr. Oketch's wrath. However, Mr. Oketch seeks out the perpetrator in a chilling yet comical outcome.

movies.title: The World
movies.description: The World was inspired by a conversation between director Jia Zhang-ke and star Zhao Tao ( Caught by the Tides ) about the latter’s experience working as a dancer at Shenzhen’s “Window of The World,” a theme park filled with miniature versions of international landmarks. In his first film made with the approval of the Chinese government, Jia explores the role of theme parks in altering contemporary national identity-construction, and blurring the line between reality and fantasy. Following a cast of rural migrants working at the park in the early 20th century, he depicts their experience of faux freedom in a pointed commentary on the implications of globalization.

movies.title: The Yellow Sea
movies.description: Jang and Lee Byung-hoon’s propulsive score sets a fire under Na’s unrelenting man-on-the-run thriller that burns hotter with each passing minute. Debt-strapped down-on-his-luck cabbie Gu-nam (Ha Jung-woo), an ethnic Korean living and working in China,…

movies.title: Three Crowns Of The Sailor
movies.description: Prolific Chilean director Raúl Ruiz’s 1982 magical realist film is a spellbinding labyrinth of stories within stories, a ghostly maritime fable that drifts between an ocean vessel and the far reaches of memory. When a desperate student encounters a mysterious sailor marked for death, he’s drawn into a nocturnal voyage of uncanny encounters, temporal slips, and philosophical riddles. Laced with Ruiz’s sly wit and oneiric logic, this cult classic is a hypnotic meditation on the porous border between life and afterlife.

movies.title: Tidal Memory
movies.description: Programmed by Melissa Lyde Positioned as a counter-narrative to a celebration of the 250th anniversary of the founding of the United States, Tidal Memory asks what it means to remember through water—where the “afterlives of slavery” continue to shape Black life, ecological systems, and the conditions we live within today. Considering the Atlantic Ocean and other bodies of water as living archives shaped by the Transatlantic Slave Trade, this series—curated by Alfreda’s Cinema—draws on the work of Christina Sharpe to explore how histories of forced migration, extraction, and loss remain materially present in the environment.

movies.title: Time and Tide
movies.description: Back in Hong Kong after taking his shot at conquering Hollywood, Tsui returned home with both barrels blazing, producing this high-strung action melodrama about a cash-strapped expectant father (Nicholas Tse) who joins the bodyguard service of his uncle…

movies.title: To A Land Unknown
movies.description: Palestinian cousins Chatila and Reda are saving to pay for fake passports to get out of Athens. But when Reda loses their hard-earned cash to his dangerous drug addiction, Chatila hatches an extreme plan, which involves them posing as smugglers and taking hostages in an effort to get out of their hopeless environment before it is too late.

movies.title: To Sleep With Anger
movies.description: A slow-burning masterwork of the early 1990s, this third feature by L.A. Rebellion’s Charles Burnett is a singular piece of American mythmaking. In a towering performance, Danny Glover plays the enigmatic southern drifter Harry, a devilish charmer who turns up out of the blue on the doorstep of old friends in South Central Los Angeles. In short order, Harry’s presence seems to cast a chaotic spell on what appeared to be a peaceful household, exposing smoldering tensions between parents and children, tradition and change, virtue and temptation. Interweaving evocative strains of gospel and blues with rich, poetic-realist images, this modern tale of the Great Migration is a sublimely stirring film from an autonomous artistic sensibility, a portrait of family resilience steeped in the traditions of African American mysticism and folklore.

movies.title: To Sleep With Anger

In a towering performance, Danny Glover plays the enigmatic southern drifter Harry, a devilish charmer who turns up out of the blue on the doorstep of old friends in South Central Los Angeles.
